title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
御史率以入院登堂肅衆曰
是役也
朝廷求賢之科學士發身之途
也庸私且怠非惟失士乃上
負
聖天子衆其念哉所不精白旣厥
心者有如皦日旣飭簾内外
===
惟謹遂進巡按陝西監察御
史邢〔尚簡〕提學副使顧〔四科〕
所選士二千五百有奇三試
之拔其儁六十有五人列名
氏弁録其文之粹者旣成書
將
獻〔履中〕乃作而敘曰維兹雍域
punctuated: 御史率以入院，登堂肅衆曰：「是役也，朝廷求賢之科，學士發身之途也。庸私且怠，非惟失士，乃上負聖天子。衆其念哉！所不精白旣厥心者，有如皦日！」旣飭簾内外惟謹，遂進巡按陝西監察御史邢〔尚簡〕、提學副使顧〔四科〕所選士二千五百有奇，三試之，拔其儁六十有五人，列名氏，弁録其文之粹者。旣成書，將獻，〔履中〕乃作而敘曰：「維兹雍域
translation_en: …The censor led them into the examination compound, ascended the hall, and called the assembly to order, saying: “This undertaking is the court’s examination for seeking worthy men and the scholars’ path to advancement. To act with partiality and negligence would not merely mean failing to obtain worthy scholars; it would also mean betraying the sagely Son of Heaven above us. Let everyone bear this in mind! Should anyone fail to make his heart wholly pure [?], let the bright sun bear witness!” Having strictly admonished those both inside and outside the examination curtain, they then admitted the more than 2,500 scholars selected by Xing Shangjian 邢尚簡, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Shaanxi, and Gu Sike 顧四科, Vice Commissioner for Education Intendancy. They examined them in three sessions and selected sixty-five of the most outstanding. Their names were listed at the front of the record, and the finest of their compositions were recorded. title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
天地之所開先是故蓄精發
輿神聖迭生其在輔世若皐
益伊呂周召光昭萬世無尚
次若秉時策勳于今輝映簡
編者亦代不乏人所謂誕奇
之靈區而產材之巨藪也非
乎〔履中〕始有知識即聞天下
有關中之勝而竊寐成紀豐
鎬者有年迺今幸覩華嶽終
南之巨
===
天都而崑崙大河之有源委信壯
遊也既得讀多士之文倬乎
岸嵂浩乎汪洋往往與河山
比盛此其甲天下士者耶夫
punctuated: 天地之所開先，是故蓄精發輿，神聖迭生。其在輔世，若皐、益、伊、呂、周、召，光昭萬世，無尚；次若秉時策勳，于今輝映簡編者，亦代不乏人。所謂誕奇之靈區，而產材之巨藪也，非乎？〔履中〕始有知識，即聞天下有關中之勝，而竊寐成紀、豐、鎬者有年。迺今幸覩華嶽、終南之巨，天都而崑崙、大河之有源委，信壯遊也。既得讀多士之文，倬乎岸嵂，浩乎汪洋，往往與河山比盛，此其甲天下士者耶？夫
translation_en:
…where Heaven and Earth first began their work of creation. Thus it stores up vital essence and brings it forth [?], and divine sages arise in succession. Among those who assisted in governing the world were Gao Yao, Yi, Yi Yin, Lü Shang, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao: their radiance shines through myriad generations, unsurpassed. Below them, those who grasped the opportunities of their times and won recorded merit, whose deeds still illuminate the historical annals, have likewise been plentiful in every age. Is this not what is called a numinous region that brings forth extraordinary people, a vast gathering ground that produces talent?
I, 〔Lüzhong〕, heard of the splendor of Guanzhong as soon as I began to understand the world, and for years privately dreamed of Chengji, Feng, and Hao. Now, fortunately, I have seen the grandeur of Mount Hua and Mount Zhongnan, the heavenly capital [?], and Kunlun and the sources and courses of the Great River. Truly, this has been a magnificent journey. Having also had the opportunity to read the writings of the many candidates—lofty as towering peaks, vast as the boundless waters—I find that they often rival the rivers and mountains in splendor. Are these, then, the men who rank foremost among the scholars of the realm? Now, …

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
部右侍郎謝〔蘭〕保釐底績文
事聿興今右副都御史傅〔鳳〕
〔翔〕交承撫綏嘉樂登俊巡撫
延綏右僉都御史楊〔守謙〕寧
夏右僉都御史先王〔邦瑞〕今
張〔鎬〕甘肅右僉都御史楊〔愽〕
撫治鄖陽右僉都御史任〔瀛〕
===
胥敉彝憲振起士風巡茶監
察御史先盛〔汝謙〕今劉〔崙〕巡
鹽監察御史劉〔應熊〕風紀丕
揚士習以正督造太監孟〔忠〕
總兵署都督僉事成〔勳〕戶部
郎中王〔太平〕王〔光宇〕有事玆
土樂觀成事右布政使徐〔守〕
punctuated: 部右侍郎謝〔蘭〕保釐底績，文事聿興。今右副都御史傅〔鳳〕〔翔〕交承撫綏，嘉樂登俊。巡撫延綏右僉都御史楊〔守謙〕、寧夏右僉都御史先王〔邦瑞〕今張〔鎬〕、甘肅右僉都御史楊〔愽〕、撫治鄖陽右僉都御史任〔瀛〕，胥敉彝憲，振起士風。巡茶監察御史先盛〔汝謙〕今劉〔崙〕、巡鹽監察御史劉〔應熊〕，風紀丕揚，士習以正。督造太監孟〔忠〕、總兵署都督僉事成〔勳〕、戶部郎中王〔太平〕、王〔光宇〕，有事玆土，樂觀成事。右布政使徐〔守〕
translation_en: …Xie Lan, Right Vice Minister of the ministry [name missing], achieved results in maintaining order, and literary pursuits flourished. The present Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, Fu Fengxiang, succeeded him in pacifying and caring for the region, gladly promoting talented men. Yang Shouqian, Grand Coordinator of Yansui and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief; the successive Right Assistant Censors-in-Chief in Ningxia, formerly Wang Bangrui and now Zhang Gao; Yang Bo, Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief in Gansu; and Ren Ying, Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief charged with pacifying and administering Yunyang, all upheld the established statutes and invigorated the ethos of the scholars. The successive Investigating Censors inspecting the tea administration, formerly Sheng Ruqian and now Liu Lun, together with Liu Yingxiong, Investigating Censor inspecting the salt administration, greatly strengthened discipline, thereby rectifying the scholars’ conduct. Meng Zhong, the Grand Eunuch supervising construction; Cheng Xun, Regional Commander and acting Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief; and Wang Taiping and Wang Guangyu, Bureau Directors in the Ministry of Revenue, had duties in this territory and were pleased to witness the undertaking’s successful completion. 叅政張愚江東謝存儒王儀
左叅議李維藩右叅議劉世
用副使茅盤郭朝賓王廷李
磐石永劉儒朱用張鈇江濬

===

translation_en:
Shaanxi Provincial Examination, the twenty-eighth year of Jiajing (1549)

Supervising Official
Cheng Yue, Regional Inspecting Censor for Shaanxi, had the courtesy name Xinfu and was from Linqing Subprefecture, Shandong. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the wuxu year.

Proctors
Ge Shouli, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shaanxi, had the courtesy name Yuli and was from Deping County, Shandong. He became a metropolitan graduate in the jichou year.
Li Yankang, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner of Shaanxi, had the courtesy name Yunji and was from Changzhi County, Shanxi. He became a metropolitan graduate in the renchen year.

Examination Inspectors
Jia Yingchun, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Shaanxi, had the courtesy name Dongyang and was from Zhending County in the directly administered territory (Zhili). He became a metropolitan graduate in the guiwei year.
Meng Yan, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner of Shaanxi, had the courtesy name Ruxue and was from Zezhou Subprefecture, Shanxi. He became a metropolitan graduate in the wuxu year.

Examiners
Qiu Lüzhong, Instructor in the Confucian School of Puzhou Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, had the courtesy name Boshi and was from Taicang Subprefecture, Zhili. He was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the dingyou year.
Lu Kui, Instructor in the Confucian School of Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, had the courtesy name Ziwen and was from Qizhou Subprefecture, Huguang. He was a tribute scholar of the guimao year.

Associate Examiners
Ma Maoyuan, Instructor in the Confucian School of Daming Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Renqing and was from Shanzhou Subprefecture, Henan. He was a tribute scholar of the xinmao year.
Wang Chen, Instructor in the Confucian School of Huguan County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi, had the courtesy name Yizhan. He was registered with the Imperial Medical Service, was originally from Yongfeng County, Jiangxi, and was a tribute scholar of the guimao year.
Cai Ruhan, Instructor in the Confucian School of Wannian County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Ziyan and was from Raoping County, Guangdong. He was a tribute scholar of the guimao year.
Xiong Shiying, Instructor in the Confucian School of Fugou County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Wenhua. He was registered with Bijie Guard, Guizhou, was originally from Tongcheng County, Huguang, and was a tribute scholar of the bingwu year.
Wei Xigu, Instructor in the Confucian School of Ganyu County, Haizhou Subprefecture, Huai’an Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Ruxue and was from Guilin Central Guard, Guangxi. He was a tribute scholar of the guimao year.

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
多聞擇其善者而從之多見而識之知之
次也
誠身有道不明乎善不誠乎身矣
夫志氣之帥也氣體之充也夫志至焉氣
次焉故曰持其志無暴其氣
易
大君有命以正功也
===
六二鴻漸于磐飲食衎衎吉
乾以易知坤以簡能易則易知簡則易從
易知則有親易從則有功有親則可久
有功則可大可久則賢人之德可大則
賢人之業易簡而天下之理得矣天下
之理得而成位乎其中矣
六爻相雜唯其時物也
書
惟動丕應徯志以昭受上帝天其申命用
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

多聞，擇其善者而從之；多見而識之，知之次也。

誠身有道：不明乎善，不誠乎身矣。

夫志，氣之帥也；氣，體之充也。夫志至焉，氣次焉。故曰：「持其志，無暴其氣。」

易

大君有命，以正功也。

六二：鴻漸于磐，飲食衎衎，吉。

乾以易知，坤以簡能。易則易知，簡則易從；易知則有親，易從則有功；有親則可久，有功則可大；可久則賢人之德，可大則賢人之業。易簡而天下之理得矣；天下之理得，而成位乎其中矣。

六爻相雜，唯其時物也。

書

惟動丕應徯志，以昭受上帝。天其申命用
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Hear much, select what is good and follow it; see much and retain it in memory. This is the next best thing to knowledge.

There is a way to make oneself sincere: without understanding goodness, one cannot make oneself sincere.

The will is the commander of the vital energy (qi); vital energy fills the body. The will comes first, and vital energy comes second. Thus it is said: “Hold firm to your will, and do not do violence to your vital energy.”

Book of Changes

“The great ruler issues commands”: this is to assess achievements justly.

Six in the second place: the wild goose gradually advances to a rock. Eating and drinking in contentment. Auspicious.

Qian directs through ease; Kun accomplishes through simplicity. What is easy is easy to understand; what is simple is easy to follow. What is easy to understand wins affection; what is easy to follow produces achievement. With affection, one can endure; with achievement, one can become great. Endurance is the virtue of the worthy; greatness is the undertaking of the worthy. Through ease and simplicity, the principles of all under Heaven are grasped. When those principles are grasped, one establishes one’s place in their midst.

The six lines intermingle, according to the times and circumstances they represent.

Book of Documents

In your actions, respond fully to the aspirations of those who await you, so as illustriously to receive the mandate of the Lord on High. Heaven will renew its mandate, thereby …

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
休
若金用汝作礪若濟巨川用汝作舟楫若
歲大旱用汝作霖雨
初一曰五行
文王惟克厥宅心乃克立茲常事司牧人
以克俊有德
詩
樹之榛栗椅桐梓漆爰伐琴瑟
吉甫燕喜既多受祉來歸自鎬我行永久
飲御諸友炰鼈膾鯉侯誰在矣張仲孝
===
友
于周受命自召祖命
赫赫厥聲濯濯厥靈壽考且寧以保我後
生
春秋
柔會宋公陳侯蔡叔盟于折　公會宋公
于夫鍾　冬十有二月公會宋公于闞
俱桓公十有一年　公會宋公于虛　冬
punctuated:
休。

若金，用汝作礪；若濟巨川，用汝作舟楫；若歲大旱，用汝作霖雨。

初一曰五行。

文王惟克厥宅心，乃克立茲常事司牧人，以克俊有德。

詩

樹之榛栗，椅桐梓漆，爰伐琴瑟。

吉甫燕喜，既多受祉。來歸自鎬，我行永久。飲御諸友，炰鼈膾鯉。侯誰在矣？張仲孝友。

于周受命，自召祖命。

赫赫厥聲，濯濯厥靈。壽考且寧，以保我後生。

春秋

柔會宋公、陳侯、蔡叔，盟于折。公會宋公于夫鍾。冬十有二月，公會宋公于闞。俱桓公十有一年。公會宋公于虛。冬，
translation_en:
…favor.

If I am metal, I will use you as my whetstone; if I cross a great river, I will use you as my boat and oars; if the year brings a great drought, I will use you as a soaking rain.

The first is called the Five Phases.

King Wen could set his heart firmly in its proper place; thus he could establish these regular offices and shepherd the people, employing men of outstanding virtue.

Book of Odes

Plant hazels and chestnuts, yi trees, tong trees, catalpas, and lacquer trees, to be felled for making zithers.

Jifu feasts in joy, having received abundant blessings. Returning from Hao, I have been away on campaign for a very long time. Friends are served drink, with roasted turtles and sliced carp. Who is present? Zhang Zhong, filial and devoted to his brothers.

Receive your charge at Zhou, following the charge given to your ancestor, the Duke of Shao.

Illustrious is your fame, splendid your spiritual power. May you live long and in peace, protecting us who come after.

Spring and Autumn Annals

Rou met with the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, and Shu of Cai; they concluded a covenant at Zhe. The duke met with the Duke of Song at Fuzhong. In winter, in the twelfth month, the duke met with the Duke of Song at Kan. These entries all belong to the eleventh year of Duke Huan. The duke met with the Duke of Song at Xu. In winter …

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
十有一月公會宋公于龜〔俱桓公十有二年〕
秋九月齊侯宋公江人黄人盟于貫〔僖公二年〕
六月公會宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯晉趙盾癸酉同盟于新城〔文公十有四年〕
春王正月季孫宿叔老會晉士匄齊人宋人衛人鄭公孫蠆曹人莒人邾人滕人
薛人杞人小邾人會吳于向〔二月□□〕
叔孫豹會晉荀偃齊人宋人衛北宫括
鄭公孫蠆曹人莒人邾人滕人薛人杞
人小邾人伐秦　冬季孫宿會晉士匄
宋華閲衛孫林父鄭公孫蠆莒人邾人
于戚〔俱襄公十有四年〕
禮記
命大師陳詩以觀民風
大羹不和貴其質也大圭不琢美其質也
punctuated:
十有一月，公會宋公于龜。〔俱桓公十有二年〕秋九月，齊侯、宋公、江人、黄人盟于貫。〔僖公二年〕六月，公會宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、晉趙盾，癸酉，同盟于新城。〔文公十有四年〕春，王正月，季孫宿、叔老會晉士匄、齊人、宋人、衛人、鄭公孫蠆、曹人、莒人、邾人、滕人、薛人、杞人、小邾人，會吳于向。〔二月□□〕叔孫豹會晉荀偃、齊人、宋人、衛北宫括、鄭公孫蠆、曹人、莒人、邾人、滕人、薛人、杞人、小邾人伐秦。冬，季孫宿會晉士匄、宋華閲、衛孫林父、鄭公孫蠆、莒人、邾人于戚。〔俱襄公十有四年〕

禮記
命大師陳詩，以觀民風。
大羹不和，貴其質也；大圭不琢，美其質也。
translation_en:
…In the eleventh month, the duke met the Duke of Song at Gui. 〔Both entries date to the twelfth year of Duke Huan.〕 In autumn, in the ninth month, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and representatives of Jiang and Huang concluded a covenant at Guan. 〔The second year of Duke Xi.〕 In the sixth month, the duke met the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, and Zhao Dun of Jin. On the guiyou day, they jointly concluded a covenant at Xincheng. 〔The fourteenth year of Duke Wen.〕 In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, Jisun Su and Shu Lao joined Shi Gai of Jin, representatives of Qi, Song, and Wei, Gongsun Chai of Zheng, and representatives of Cao, Ju, Zhu, Teng, Xue, Qi, and Lesser Zhu to meet Wu at Xiang. 〔Second month, □□ [?].〕 Shusun Bao joined Xun Yan of Jin, representatives of Qi and Song, Beigong Kuo of Wei, Gongsun Chai of Zheng, and representatives of Cao, Ju, Zhu, Teng, Xue, Qi, and Lesser Zhu in attacking Qin. In winter, Jisun Su met Shi Gai of Jin, Hua Yue of Song, Sun Linfu of Wei, Gongsun Chai of Zheng, and representatives of Ju and Zhu at Qi. 〔All date to the fourteenth year of Duke Xiang.〕

Book of Rites
The Grand Music Master is ordered to present poems so that the customs of the people may be observed.
The great sacrificial broth is left unseasoned because its natural substance is valued; the great jade tablet is left uncarved because its natural substance is considered beautiful.

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
禮樂之說管乎人情矣
夫孝置之而塞乎天地溥之而横乎四海
施諸後世而無朝夕推而放諸東海而
凖推而放諸西海而凖推而放諸南海
而凖推而放諸北海而凖詩云自西自
東自南自北無思不服此之謂也
第貳場
論
君子深造之以道
===
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢春和議賑貸詔〔文帝元年〕
擬唐以魏徵爲太子太師誥〔貞觀十六年〕
擬宋賜輔臣御製瑞聖園觀稼城南觀麥
詩謝表〔祥符九年〕
判語〔五條〕
官吏給由
收養孤老
奏對失序
punctuated:
禮樂之說，管乎人情矣。
夫孝，置之而塞乎天地，溥之而横乎四海，施諸後世而無朝夕。推而放諸東海而凖，推而放諸西海而凖，推而放諸南海而凖，推而放諸北海而凖。《詩》云：「自西自東，自南自北，無思不服。」此之謂也。
第貳場
論
君子深造之以道。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢春和議賑貸詔〔文帝元年〕。
擬唐以魏徵爲太子太師誥〔貞觀十六年〕。
擬宋賜輔臣御製瑞聖園觀稼城南觀麥詩謝表〔祥符九年〕。
判語〔五條〕
官吏給由。
收養孤老。
奏對失序。
translation_en:
The teachings of ritual and music encompass human feelings.
As for filial piety, establish it and it fills heaven and earth; spread it and it extends across the Four Seas; apply it to later generations and it holds true at all times, morning and evening. Extend and apply it to the Eastern Sea, and it accords with the standard; extend and apply it to the Western Sea, and it accords with the standard; extend and apply it to the Southern Sea, and it accords with the standard; extend and apply it to the Northern Sea, and it accords with the standard. The Book of Odes says: “From the west and from the east, from the south and from the north, none fail to submit.” This is what it means.
Second Session
Discourse
“The noble man pursues profound attainment by following the Way.”
Edicts, Pronouncements, and Memorials 〔One topic from among these [?].〕
Compose an edict in the manner of the Han dynasty ordering deliberation on relief grants and loans during the mild spring. 〔First year of Emperor Wen’s reign.〕
Compose a pronouncement in the manner of the Tang dynasty appointing Wei Zheng Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent. 〔Sixteenth year of Zhenguan.〕
Compose a memorial of thanks in the manner of the Song dynasty for the bestowal upon the chief ministers of the imperially composed poems “Viewing the Crops at Ruisheng Garden” and “Viewing the Wheat South of the City.” 〔Ninth year of Xiangfu.〕
Legal Judgments 〔Five items.〕
Issuing certificates of service to officials and clerks.
Providing care for orphans and the elderly without family support.
Breaching the prescribed order when submitting reports or answering the emperor.

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
飛報軍情
聽訟迴避
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問帝王之文二曰詔令曰製作我
太祖以天縱之聖當創業之始好古右文昭
一人之大制渙天下之至文千古獨盛矣試竊
舉所知一二與爾諸士闡揚之以言乎
詔令也諭安南有
===
詔諭雲南有
詔有赦宥之
詔有存恤之
詔或諭刑官或諭審決或
親諭舉到人材或
詔免天下田租其文煥然與洛四岳諸典同歸
矣可得而各撮其要與以言乎
製作也則有七曜循環之論有鬼神有無之論
有時雪之篇有春光之篇問心有擬省
punctuated:
飛報軍情。
聽訟迴避。

第叁場
策〔五道〕

問：帝王之文二：曰詔令，曰製作。我太祖以天縱之聖，當創業之始，好古右文，昭一人之大制，渙天下之至文，千古獨盛矣。試竊舉所知一二，與爾諸士闡揚之。以言乎詔令也，諭安南有詔，諭雲南有詔，有赦宥之詔，有存恤之詔，或諭刑官，或諭審決，或親諭舉到人材，或詔免天下田租，其文煥然，與洛四岳諸典同歸矣，可得而各撮其要與？以言乎製作也，則有七曜循環之論，有鬼神有無之論，有時雪之篇，有春光之篇，問心有擬，省
translation_en:
Urgent reporting of military intelligence.
Recusal in hearing lawsuits.

Third Session
Policy Questions〔Five questions〕

Question: The writings of emperors and kings are of two kinds: edicts and commands, and literary compositions. At the beginning of his dynastic undertaking, our Taizu, with his Heaven-endowed sagacity, cherished antiquity and promoted letters. He made manifest the sovereign’s great ordinances and disseminated the finest writings throughout the realm, achieving a splendor unmatched through the ages. Let us venture to cite one or two examples we know, so that you candidates may elucidate them.

Regarding edicts and commands, there are edicts instructing Annan and Yunnan, edicts granting pardons, and edicts providing relief and care. Some instruct judicial officials; others give directions concerning judicial review and decisions. Some personally instruct men of talent who have been recommended and brought to court; others remit land taxes throughout the realm. These writings are resplendent, sharing the purport of the classical texts concerning Luo and the Four Chiefs [?]. Can you summarize the essentials of each?

Regarding literary compositions, there are discourses on the cycles of the Seven Luminaries and on the existence or nonexistence of ghosts and spirits, and pieces on timely snow and the light of spring. On questioning the heart there is an imitative composition; sheng [the next phrase is incomplete and unclear]…

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
頒有文保身有說勤惰有說其詞燦然
與勅天命諸歌並美矣不審能盡達其
旨與二者之文亦各有所本與我
皇上聖智之資同符
聖祖經綸之作于前有光如
大享禮成詔
大狩龍飛錄敬一箴四箴註仲夏寫懷之什欽
天記頌之作其旨其本復可得而知與夫
聖人有作而臣民不知恥也生今之世而昧今
===
之典非士也爾諸士固菁莪樸棫中人
矣幸齋心滌慮相與敬陳之勿忽
問六經聖人致治之迹也炳如日星以詔
後世自宋儒理學闡明易程朱書蔡氏
詩朱子春秋胡氏禮陳灝令世宗之自
漢以降經師有不能識其名者果諸䟽
傳訓詁可盡廢耶易有田何焦贛費直
數傳之後王弼爲注說者謂爲老易何
歟書有孔惠伏勝武帝之時屋壁之藏
punctuated:
頒有文，保身有說，勤惰有說，其詞燦然，與勅天命諸歌並美矣。不審能盡達其旨與？二者之文亦各有所本與？我皇上聖智之資，同符聖祖，經綸之作，于前有光。如《大享禮成詔》《大狩龍飛錄》《敬一箴》《四箴註》《仲夏寫懷》之什、《欽天記頌》之作，其旨其本，復可得而知與？夫聖人有作而臣民不知，恥也；生今之世而昧今之典，非士也。爾諸士固菁莪樸棫中人矣，幸齋心滌慮，相與敬陳之，勿忽！
問：六經，聖人致治之迹也，炳如日星，以詔後世。自宋儒理學闡明，《易》程朱，《書》蔡氏，《詩》朱子，《春秋》胡氏，《禮》陳灝，令世宗之。自漢以降，經師有不能識其名者，果諸䟽傳訓詁可盡廢耶？《易》有田何、焦贛、費直，數傳之後，王弼爲注，說者謂爲老易，何歟？《書》有孔惠、伏勝，武帝之時，屋壁之藏
translation_en:
…there is a composition on promulgation [?], a discussion of preserving oneself, and a discussion of diligence and indolence. Their language shines brilliantly, rivaling in beauty the songs concerning admonition and Heaven’s mandate [?]. Can you fully comprehend their purport? Do these two categories of writings each have a foundation?
Our Emperor’s endowment of sagely wisdom accords with that of the Sagely Progenitor, and his writings on ordering the realm add luster to those of his predecessor. Examples include the Edict on the Completion of the Great Sacrificial Rite, the Record of the Great Hunt and the Dragon’s Ascent [?], the Admonition on Reverent Unity, the Commentary on the Four Admonitions, the verses Expressing My Feelings in Midsummer, and the composition Record and Eulogy of Revering Heaven [?]. Can their purport and foundations likewise be ascertained? When a sage produces writings and his subjects do not know them, it is shameful. To live in the present age yet remain ignorant of its authoritative texts is unworthy of a scholar. You scholars surely belong among those celebrated in the Odes “Luxuriant Southernwood” and “The Oaks,” nurtured and cultivated as worthy men. Purify your minds and cleanse your thoughts; together, respectfully set forth your answers. Do not be negligent!
Question: The Six Classics are the traces left by the sages in bringing about good government. Brilliant as the sun and stars, they instruct later generations. Since the Song Confucians elucidated the learning of principle, Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi on the Changes, Cai on the Documents, Master Zhu on the Odes, Hu on the Spring and Autumn Annals, and Chen Hao on the Rites have been made the authorities for the world to follow. Among the classical masters from the Han onward are some whose names people cannot even recognize. Can all their subcommentaries, commentaries, and explanations of words really be discarded?
For the Changes there were Tian He, Jiao Gan, and Fei Zhi. After several generations of transmission, Wang Bi wrote a commentary. Critics call it a Laozi-inspired Changes. Why is this? For the Documents there were Kong Hui [?] and Fu Sheng. In the time of Emperor Wu, the texts hidden within the walls of a house…

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
既出孔安國以隸古定之說者謂舜典
獨闕何歟詩有申公轅固韓嬰自毛傳
之行而三家微韓詩雖在恐非美刺之
旨矣禮失而求之野后戴諸儒補綴成
篇三鄭王肅尤精其學不可盡謂之附
會也春秋鄒夾之學漢已無傳左氏穀
梁公羊三家詞旨各異則夫表章尊信
參別異同當何所折衷哉或者去古未
遠擬之臆決於千百載之下者恐相懸
也諸生明經既有年矣試陳其槩以驗
===
博綜古今之蘊
問生民休戚係守令之賢否以職親而澤
易究耳自古以來表循良於史冊代不
乏人獨稱漢世為盛何與今列傳所載
其人與政班班可考可歷指而言之與
史稱文景之世吏安其官民樂其業當
時未聞以循吏稱嗣是厥後吏治競為
苛刻離散民心斲喪元氣由是循吏出
punctuated:
既出，孔安國以隸古定之，說者謂舜典獨闕，何歟？詩有申公、轅固、韓嬰，自毛傳之行而三家微，韓詩雖在，恐非美刺之旨矣。禮失而求之野，后戴諸儒補綴成篇，三鄭、王肅尤精其學，不可盡謂之附會也。春秋鄒夾之學，漢已無傳，左氏、穀梁、公羊三家詞旨各異，則夫表章尊信、參別異同，當何所折衷哉？或者去古未遠，擬之臆決於千百載之下者，恐相懸也。諸生明經既有年矣，試陳其槩，以驗博綜古今之蘊。
問：生民休戚係守令之賢否，以職親而澤易究耳。自古以來，表循良於史冊，代不乏人，獨稱漢世為盛，何與？今列傳所載，其人與政班班可考，可歷指而言之與？史稱文景之世，吏安其官，民樂其業，當時未聞以循吏稱。嗣是厥後，吏治競為苛刻，離散民心，斲喪元氣，由是循吏出
translation_en:
…once these had come to light, Kong Anguo established the text by rendering the ancient script into clerical script. Commentators say that the Canon of Shun alone was missing. Why was this? For the Book of Odes there were Shen Gong, Yuan Gu, and Han Ying. After Mao’s Commentary came into circulation, the three other schools declined. Although the Han tradition of the Odes survives, it may not preserve the purport of their praise and criticism. When ritual learning was lost, it was sought among the common people. Hou Dai [?] and other scholars assembled and supplemented the material into chapters. The three Zheng scholars [?] and Wang Su were especially accomplished in this learning; their work cannot all be dismissed as forced interpretation. The Zou and Jia traditions of the Spring and Autumn Annals already lacked transmitters in the Han. The three traditions of Zuo, Guliang, and Gongyang differ in wording and meaning. In giving them prominence and authority, and in comparing and distinguishing their similarities and differences, what should serve as the standard of judgment? Some of these scholars lived not far from antiquity; compared with those who make conjectural judgments hundreds or thousands of years later, they may stand far apart. You students have already spent years elucidating the classics. Set out the broad outlines, so that we may assess the depth of your comprehensive learning concerning past and present.
Question: The well-being or suffering of the people depends on whether prefects and magistrates are worthy, for their offices bring them close to the people and enable their beneficence to reach them readily. Since antiquity, no dynasty has lacked men celebrated in historical records as conscientious and benevolent administrators. Why, then, is the Han alone acclaimed as having had them in greatest abundance? The men and their administrations recorded in the biographies can be clearly examined. Can you identify and discuss them one by one? The histories state that under Emperors Wen and Jing, officials were secure in their offices and the people content in their occupations. Yet at that time we do not hear of officials singled out as exemplary administrators. Thereafter, officials competed in harshness in their administration, alienating the people’s hearts and sapping the realm’s vital energies. Thus exemplary administrators emerged…

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
焉而俗吏習猶未已觀於章帝詔戒可
知其稱循吏安靜不擾悃愊無華乃木
强之人而止耳當時何所導化而民安
之何所據依而殿最之與方今談龔黃
之化理罔不慨然嚮慕迺吏習骫靡愈
趨愈下將何脩而可以挽回古之休風
與說者謂文景之世居官者長子孫以
爲姓氏今弊在數易邇來當塗之士建
議久任夥矣卒不果行豈古之法不可
行於今與抑别有其故與諸士子行將
服官理民幸昌言之勿讓
===
問地靈人傑理所不誣關隴之產可稽矣
粤若神聖詩書所稱不俟名言其他多
才多藝吏僕未易盡數姑以漢唐而下
功在社稷名流邊徼經術相授節介獨
行表著簡冊者舉而詢之多士可乎且
如總領衆職雅與丙吉同心裁處無滯
善資玄齡之斷以至正直行而天下以
punctuated:
焉，而俗吏習猶未已，觀於章帝詔戒可知。其稱循吏安靜不擾，悃愊無華，乃木强之人而止耳。當時何所導化而民安之？何所據依而殿最之與？方今談龔黃之化理，罔不慨然嚮慕，迺吏習骫靡，愈趨愈下。將何脩而可以挽回古之休風與？說者謂文景之世，居官者長子孫以爲姓氏，今弊在數易。邇來當塗之士建議久任夥矣，卒不果行，豈古之法不可行於今與？抑别有其故與？諸士子行將服官理民，幸昌言之，勿讓。

問：地靈人傑，理所不誣，關隴之產可稽矣。粤若神聖，詩書所稱，不俟名言。其他多才多藝，吏僕未易盡數。姑以漢唐而下，功在社稷，名流邊徼，經術相授，節介獨行，表著簡冊者，舉而詢之多士，可乎？且如總領衆職，雅與丙吉同心；裁處無滯，善資玄齡之斷；以至正直行而天下以
translation_en:
…emerged, yet the habits of ordinary officials still persisted, as can be seen from Emperor Zhang’s admonitory edict. Those it calls conscientious officials were quiet and peaceable, causing no disturbance, sincere and unadorned—merely plain, unbending men. By what means did they guide and transform the people at that time, so that the people lived contentedly under them? On what grounds were they assessed as inferior or superior? Nowadays, whenever people discuss the transformative government of Gong and Huang, all express ardent admiration; yet official habits grow lax and degenerate, sinking ever lower. What must be cultivated to restore the admirable customs of antiquity? Some say that in the reigns of Emperors Wen and Jing, officeholders remained long enough to raise children and grandchildren, taking their offices as family names, whereas today the harm lies in frequent replacement. Recently, many men in positions of authority have proposed long tenures, but these proposals have ultimately not been implemented. Can ancient methods not be practiced today, or is there some other reason? You candidates will soon hold office and govern the people. Please speak fully and frankly, without hesitation.

Question: That a region’s spiritual potency produces outstanding men is a principle that does not deceive us; the men born in Guanlong furnish evidence. As for the divine sages celebrated in the Odes and the Documents, there is no need to name them. The other men of many talents and accomplishments—the officials and servants [?]—cannot readily be counted in full. May we select, from the Han and Tang onward, those whose achievements benefited the altars of soil and grain, whose fame spread to the frontiers, who transmitted classical learning, or whose integrity and exceptional conduct were recorded prominently in the histories, and question you candidates about them? Consider, for example, the man who oversaw the various offices and was consistently of one mind with Bing Ji; the man who handled affairs without delay and ably drew upon Xuanling’s decisiveness; and further, the man through whom upright conduct prevailed and All-under-Heaven thereby…

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
肥渡河決而澶淵取勝皆相業之卓然
者也孰爲最乎屯隍中而服罟开入虎
穴而質鄯善至於大振軍威以身爲天
下安危用師無祀棄家以再造社稷皆
威武之傑然者也孰爲難乎他如慱通
經籍而設帳授徒問事不休而世稱通
儒以至長曆作而武庫取名訂頑訓而
聖學丕著固皆當世之儒宗也孰近道
乎隱居谷口而清風足以勵俗牧豕上
===
林而咏詩聊以娱日以至泉石膏肓帝
幸其門而比之四皓雲溪退士帝嘉其
節而命之存問固皆一時之逸民也孰
爲固乎多士之素處固必以節介經術
相高今將頴脫而出矣出將入相亦丈
夫之所有志者也幸備論往哲歸所願
學是不忘其尚友之實有司將以審所
從也其勿曰方人不暇
問足食莫善於屯田强兵莫要於畜馬比
punctuated:
肥，渡河決而澶淵取勝，皆相業之卓然者也，孰爲最乎？屯隍中而服罟开，入虎穴而質鄯善，至於大振軍威，以身爲天下安危；用師無祀，棄家以再造社稷，皆威武之傑然者也，孰爲難乎？他如慱通經籍而設帳授徒，問事不休而世稱通儒，以至長曆作而武庫取名，訂頑訓而聖學丕著，固皆當世之儒宗也，孰近道乎？隱居谷口而清風足以勵俗，牧豕上林而咏詩聊以娱日，以至泉石膏肓，帝幸其門而比之四皓；雲溪退士，帝嘉其節而命之存問，固皆一時之逸民也，孰爲固乎？多士之素處，固必以節介、經術相高，今將頴脫而出矣。出將入相，亦丈夫之所有志者也。幸備論往哲，歸所願學，是不忘其尚友之實。有司將以審所從也，其勿曰方人不暇！
問：足食莫善於屯田，强兵莫要於畜馬，比
translation_en:
…flourished; and the decision to cross the river brought victory at Chanyuan. These were all outstanding achievements in the chief councillorship. Which was the greatest? Garrisoning Huangzhong [?] and subduing the tribes [?], entering the tiger’s den and taking Shanshan hostage, and, beyond these, greatly enhancing military prestige so that the security or peril of the realm depended on one man; campaigning against those who neglected the sacrifices [?], and abandoning one’s family to restore the state: these were all exceptional feats of martial prowess. Which was the most difficult? Others mastered the classical writings and established schools to teach disciples, or inquired tirelessly into affairs and became celebrated as comprehensive scholars. Still others compiled the Long Calendar and earned the name “Arsenal,” or expounded the Admonition to the Obtuse (Dingwan), making the learning of the sages brilliantly manifest. All were leading Confucian scholars of their age. Which came closest to the Way?
Some lived in seclusion at Gukou, their pure example sufficient to uplift popular custom, or herded swine at Shanglin, chanting poetry to pass the days pleasantly. Others were incurably devoted to springs and rocks: the emperor visited one at his door and compared him to the Four Hoary Elders; another was the retired scholar of Yunxi, whose integrity the emperor praised, ordering that inquiries be made after his welfare. All were recluses of their time. Which was the most steadfast?
You candidates, in your ordinary lives, must surely have sought to excel one another in integrity and classical learning. Now you are about to emerge and distinguish yourselves. To serve as generals in the field and chief councillors at court is also an aspiration proper to a man of resolve. Please discuss these worthy predecessors fully and conclude by identifying those whom you wish to emulate. This will show that you have not forgotten the substance of taking the ancients as your friends. The responsible officials will thereby examine whom you choose to follow. Do not say that you have no leisure to judge others!
Question: For ensuring sufficient food, nothing surpasses agricultural colonies; for strengthening the army, nothing is more essential than raising horses. These [?]…

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
籌邊者之所當講也歷觀往昔或耕於
塞下或田於燉煌或屯兵金城或雜耕
渭水此古人屯田之政有可考者或牧
之於官或牧之於民或官民通牧或始
牧於官而終牧於民此古人牧馬之政
有可考者其法制之詳區畫之善可詳
言與我
國家屯田專監司之職馬政設寺苑之官立
法善矣其在今日亦有利病當講以爲
===
興革者與夫屯田膏壤猶夫舊也不知
何如而可致紅腐之積苑囿沃野猶夫
昔也不知何如而可致雲錦之富探本
塞源之論權宜救弊之方必有在也諸
士皆關輔之英籌之熟矣請著於篇以
觀經世之學
punctuated: 籌邊者之所當講也。歷觀往昔，或耕於塞下，或田於燉煌，或屯兵金城，或雜耕渭水，此古人屯田之政有可考者。或牧之於官，或牧之於民，或官民通牧，或始牧於官而終牧於民，此古人牧馬之政有可考者。其法制之詳、區畫之善，可詳言與？我國家屯田專監司之職，馬政設寺苑之官，立法善矣。其在今日，亦有利病當講以爲興革者與？夫屯田膏壤猶夫舊也，不知何如而可致紅腐之積；苑囿沃野猶夫昔也，不知何如而可致雲錦之富。探本塞源之論、權宜救弊之方，必有在也。諸士皆關輔之英，籌之熟矣，請著於篇，以觀經世之學。
translation_en:
…are matters that those planning frontier defense ought to discuss. Surveying the past, we find cultivation below the frontier fortifications, farming at Dunhuang, troops stationed to farm at Jincheng, and cultivation interspersed among the inhabitants along the Wei River. These are verifiable instances of the ancients’ military agricultural colony policies. Horses were sometimes raised by the authorities, sometimes by the people, sometimes jointly by both, and sometimes initially by the authorities and subsequently by the people. These are verifiable instances of the ancients’ horse-breeding policies. Can you explain in detail the particulars of their regulations and the merits of their arrangements?

Our dynasty assigns responsibility for military agricultural colonies specifically to the surveillance commissioners, and has established officials of courts and pasturages to administer horses. Its institutions are well conceived. Yet under present circumstances, are there benefits and defects that ought to be discussed, so that useful practices may be instituted and harmful ones abolished? The fertile soil of the military agricultural colonies remains as it was of old; how, then, can we achieve grain reserves so abundant that they redden and decay in storage? The rich fields of the pasturages remain as they were in former times; how, then, can we achieve a wealth of horses like clouds of brocade? There must be arguments that probe the roots of the problems and stop them at their source, and expedient measures that remedy abuses. You gentlemen are all outstanding talents of Guanzhong and its surrounding region, and have surely considered these matters thoroughly. Set out your views in writing, so that we may assess your learning in the art of governing.

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
多聞擇其善者而從之多見而識之知之
次也
王希堯
同考試官教諭熊　批〔聖人謙己誨人之意最難體貼是作平平發揮無一字艱澀錄之以正文體〕
同考試官教授馬　批　平正通達
考試官教諭盧　批　明淨無疵
考試官學正丘　批　平順
===
聖人自言盡求知之功亦可以近於知矣夫聖
人生而知之也乃自言其下學之功而不敢以
上知自居其亦謙已誨人之意歟其意蓋謂無
知妄作我固未甞有是矣我之所以有知者抑
豈無所本哉誠以事理之在天下惟博學能通
其故知識之在吾心必窮理斯盡其極學貴多
聞固矣多而不擇無以臻日益之效故於善者
則樂取諸人不善者在所略焉學貴多見固矣
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「多聞，擇其善者而從之；多見而識之，知之次也。」
王希堯
同考試官教諭熊批〔聖人謙己誨人之意最難體貼，是作平平發揮，無一字艱澀，錄之以正文體。〕
同考試官教授馬批：平正通達。
考試官教諭盧批：明淨無疵。
考試官學正丘批：平順。

聖人自言盡求知之功，亦可以近於知矣。夫聖人生而知之也，乃自言其下學之功，而不敢以上知自居，其亦謙已誨人之意歟？其意蓋謂：無知妄作，我固未甞有是矣。我之所以有知者，抑豈無所本哉？誠以事理之在天下，惟博學能通其故；知識之在吾心，必窮理斯盡其極。學貴多聞，固矣；多而不擇，無以臻日益之效。故於善者，則樂取諸人；不善者，在所略焉。學貴多見，固矣。
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

“Hear much, select what is good and follow it; see much and retain it in memory: this is the next best thing to knowledge.”

Wang Xiyao

Associate Examiner Xiong, Instructor, comments: 〔“The sage’s intention of humbling himself to instruct others is exceptionally difficult to grasp. This essay develops it plainly, without a single obscure word. It is included to set the prose style aright.”〕
Associate Examiner Ma, Professor, comments: “Balanced, sound, lucid, and coherent.”
Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: “Clear and pure, without blemish.”
Examiner Qiu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Balanced and fluent.”

The sage says of himself that by exerting himself fully in seeking knowledge, he too can approach knowledge. Now, the sage is born knowing; yet he speaks of his efforts in learning elementary things and does not presume to claim the highest knowledge for himself. Is this not his intention to humble himself and instruct others? His meaning is, in substance: “Acting recklessly without knowledge—I have certainly never done this. Yet could my knowledge possibly be without a foundation? Indeed, only broad learning can penetrate the reasons underlying the affairs and principles of the world; and only by investigating principles exhaustively can the knowledge in my mind reach its fullest extent. That learning values hearing much is certainly true. But hearing much without selecting cannot produce the benefit of daily improvement. Thus, whatever is good I gladly take from others; whatever is not good I pass over. That learning values seeing much is certainly true…”

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
見而不識無以備叅考之資故於善者則默識
於心惡者亦不遺焉夫多聞能擇則理有得於
所聞多見能識則理有得於所見雖未能神以
知來知以藏往與聖人之知同也造詣以強學
而進明能燭物庶幾不眩於有事矣雖未能知
周萬物旁燭無疆與生知之聖等也聰明以聞
見而廣隨事觀理庶幾不昧於所從矣不亦次
知已乎是則理以能學而明事以見理而當我
之無妄作者蓋以此耳學者其尚知所從事以
===
盡求知之功也哉抑聖人天聰明之盡一以貫
之者也何有於聞何有於見哉世固有厭進脩
爲卑近以頓悟爲超越卒之無所持循弊流於
蕩不免冥行取咎是故夫子之憂之也博約之
誘講學之憂好學之智所以惓惓不能已於言
也歟
誠身有道不明乎善不誠乎身矣
張旂
同考試官教諭廖　批〔誠明二義是篇要領此作發明〕
punctuated:
見而不識，無以備叅考之資，故於善者則默識於心，惡者亦不遺焉。夫多聞能擇，則理有得於所聞；多見能識，則理有得於所見。雖未能神以知來、知以藏往，與聖人之知同也，造詣以強學而進，明能燭物，庶幾不眩於有事矣。雖未能知周萬物、旁燭無疆，與生知之聖等也，聰明以聞見而廣，隨事觀理，庶幾不昧於所從矣。不亦次知已乎？是則理以能學而明，事以見理而當。我之無妄作者，蓋以此耳。學者其尚知所從事，以盡求知之功也哉！抑聖人天聰明之盡，一以貫之者也，何有於聞，何有於見哉？世固有厭進脩爲卑近，以頓悟爲超越，卒之無所持循，弊流於蕩，不免冥行取咎。是故夫子之憂之也，博約之誘、講學之憂、好學之智，所以惓惓不能已於言也歟？

誠身有道，不明乎善，不誠乎身矣。

張旂

同考試官教諭廖，批〔誠明二義，是篇要領，此作發明〕
translation_en:
…If one sees things without retaining them, one has no resources for comparison and examination. Thus, what is good is silently retained in the mind, while what is bad is not omitted either. By hearing much and being able to select, one grasps principle in what one hears; by seeing much and being able to retain it, one grasps principle in what one sees. Although one cannot yet use spiritual insight to know what is to come and wisdom to preserve what has passed, matching the sage’s knowledge, one’s attainment advances through diligent study. With understanding sufficient to illuminate things, one may hope to avoid confusion when affairs arise. Although one’s knowledge cannot yet encompass all things and illuminate everything without limit, equaling a sage who knows from birth, one’s intelligence expands through hearing and seeing. By observing principle in each affair, one may hope to discern the course to follow. Is this not the next level of knowledge? Thus, principle becomes clear through the ability to learn, and one’s conduct becomes fitting through perceiving principle. This, then, is why I do not act recklessly. May learners recognize where to direct their efforts and fully apply themselves to seeking knowledge!

Yet the sage possesses heavenly intelligence to its fullest extent, with a single thread running through it all. What need has he of hearing or seeing? There are certainly people who disdain progressive study and self-cultivation as lowly and commonplace, regarding sudden enlightenment as transcendent. In the end, they have nothing to uphold or follow; their failings descend into unrestrained conduct, and they inevitably act blindly and incur blame. This, then, is what concerned the Master. His encouragement to broaden learning and restrain oneself through ritual, his concern for the study and discussion of learning, and his wisdom in loving learning—were these why he spoke so earnestly and could not cease?

“There is a way to make oneself sincere: without understanding goodness, one cannot make oneself sincere.”

Zhang Qi

Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor, comments: 〔Sincerity and understanding are the two essential concepts of this essay. This composition elucidates…〕

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
意義犂然有會於心錄之
考試官教諭盧　批
辭精確而意渾融場中義似此
作者絕少
考試官學正丘　批
切理
中庸推言思誠者惟在於窮理所以明素定之
意也夫學莫先於窮理也理明則誠身之道盡
矣又豈有多術也哉中庸進哀公以誠明之學
其意蓋謂推原獲上之治固本於身之能誠欲
誠其身豈無所當豫者乎是故天命人心本自
===
無妄而知誘物化乃失其初茲欲虛中以主夫
靜所存一天理之本然無我以大其公所發皆
天則之至當要不可以襲取强爲也其道在明
善而已蓋必先明諸心知所往而不蔽於其始
然後力行以求至而克篤於其終苟格物之功
不加未能析理以致精隱微之間不免於眞妄
之錯雜也致知之力弗至未能觀物以察則趨
向之路尚涉於從違之靡定也吾見知之不眞
則爲之不力雖勉强從事終沮於他岐之惑欲
punctuated:
意義犂然，有會於心，錄之。
考試官教諭盧批：辭精確而意渾融，場中義似此作者絕少。
考試官學正丘批：切理。
中庸推言思誠者，惟在於窮理，所以明素定之意也。夫學莫先於窮理也，理明則誠身之道盡矣，又豈有多術也哉？中庸進哀公以誠明之學，其意蓋謂推原獲上之治，固本於身之能誠；欲誠其身，豈無所當豫者乎？是故天命人心，本自無妄，而知誘物化，乃失其初。茲欲虛中以主夫靜，所存一天理之本然；無我以大其公，所發皆天則之至當，要不可以襲取强爲也。其道在明善而已。蓋必先明諸心，知所往而不蔽於其始，然後力行以求至，而克篤於其終。苟格物之功不加，未能析理以致精，隱微之間不免於眞妄之錯雜也；致知之力弗至，未能觀物以察則，趨向之路尚涉於從違之靡定也。吾見知之不眞，則爲之不力，雖勉强從事，終沮於他岐之惑。欲
translation_en:
…The meaning is lucid and resonates with the mind. I select it for inclusion.
Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: “The language is precise and the meaning fully integrated. Among the essays in this examination, works like this are exceedingly rare.”
Examiner Qiu, School Instructor, comments: “It accords closely with principle.”
The Doctrine of the Mean explains that seeking sincerity rests solely upon investigating principle exhaustively, thereby elucidating the importance of being settled beforehand. In learning, nothing takes precedence over investigating principle exhaustively. Once principle is understood, the way to making oneself sincere is fully encompassed. How could it require many other methods? The Doctrine of the Mean presents Duke Ai with the teaching of sincerity and understanding. Its meaning is surely that, traced to its source, effective government through gaining the confidence of superiors rests fundamentally upon one’s ability to make oneself sincere. If one wishes to make oneself sincere, can there be nothing that must first be prepared?
Thus, the human mind as endowed by Heaven is originally free of falsity. Only when awareness is enticed and external things transform it does it lose its original condition. If one now wishes to empty the mind so as to preside over stillness, preserving solely the original condition of heavenly principle, and to eliminate the self so as to enlarge one’s impartiality, ensuring that everything issuing forth perfectly accords with Heaven’s standards, this assuredly cannot be achieved by borrowing outward forms or forcing oneself. The way lies simply in understanding goodness.
One must first attain understanding within the mind, knowing where to proceed and remaining unobscured at the outset. Only then can one strive in practice to reach the goal and remain steadfast through to the end. If one does not apply oneself to investigating things and cannot analyze principle with precision, truth and falsity will inevitably become intermingled in the hidden and subtle recesses of the mind. If one’s effort to extend knowledge falls short and one cannot observe things to discern their standards, one’s direction will still be unsettled between following and departing from those standards. I see that when knowledge is not genuine, action lacks strength. Though one forces oneself to undertake the work, one is ultimately thwarted by the bewilderment of divergent paths. To wish…

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
其眞實無妄動以天而不以人也得乎擇之不
審則行之不至雖竭力求誠終流於鹵莽之歸
欲其至善渾全去自欺而求自慊也得乎是則
誠明有合一之妙學者貴功用之全知所先後
則誠身之道盡而獲上治民可以馴致矣抑誠
明之說其聖學之心法帝王之要道乎內聖之
德外王之業要皆不外是矣是故精一而執中
緝熙而敬止風動之休怙冒之化合內外而一
之者也夫子以是告哀公其所以期望之者不
亦深且重哉然則明善之功當□□□□□□
愼思明辨中庸固已言之矣□□□□□之以
語此
===
夫志氣之帥也氣體之充也□□□□□
次焉故曰持其志無暴其氣
劉希皐
同考試官教諭蔡　批　此題作者□□□□□□□
精語新意見超然不窘
考試官教諭盧　批　辭氣沉著蓋精思而有得者
〔辭氣沉著蓋精思而有得者〕
punctuated:
其眞實無妄，動以天而不以人也，得乎？擇之不審，則行之不至，雖竭力求誠，終流於鹵莽之歸，欲其至善渾全，去自欺而求自慊也，得乎？是則誠明有合一之妙，學者貴功用之全。知所先後，則誠身之道盡，而獲上治民可以馴致矣。抑誠明之說，其聖學之心法、帝王之要道乎？內聖之德，外王之業，要皆不外是矣。是故精一而執中，緝熙而敬止，風動之休，怙冒之化，合內外而一之者也。夫子以是告哀公，其所以期望之者，不亦深且重哉？然則明善之功，當□□□□□□愼思明辨，《中庸》固已言之矣。□□□□□之以語此。

夫志，氣之帥也；氣，體之充也。□□□□□次焉。故曰：「持其志，無暴其氣。」
劉希皐

同考試官教諭蔡　批：此題作者□□□□□□□精語新，意見超然不窘。

考試官教諭盧　批：辭氣沉著，蓋精思而有得者。〔辭氣沉著，蓋精思而有得者。〕
translation_en:
…that it be genuine and free of falsity, acting according to Heaven rather than human contrivance—can this be achieved? If one's discrimination is insufficiently thorough, one's practice will fall short. Even if one exerts every effort to attain sincerity, one will ultimately lapse into heedlessness. Can one then attain goodness in its complete perfection, dispelling self-deception and seeking satisfaction within oneself? Thus sincerity and illumination possess the subtle capacity to unite as one, and learners prize completeness in their efforts. When they know what comes first and what follows, the way of making oneself sincere is fully realized; gaining the confidence of superiors and governing the people can then gradually be achieved. Is not the teaching of sincerity and illumination the essential teaching concerning the mind in the learning of the sages, and the crucial way of emperors and kings? The virtue of inward sagehood and the achievement of outward kingliness alike lie within this. Thus, being discerning and single-minded so as to hold fast to the Mean, and continually cultivating brightness so as reverently to abide in the proper place, produce the blessings of influence that moves like the wind and the transforming power of protective care: these unite the inner and outer as one. When the Master told Duke Ai this, were not his expectations for him profound and weighty? As for the effort to illuminate goodness, one should [six illegible characters] think carefully and discriminate clearly: the Doctrine of the Mean has already spoken of this. [Five illegible characters] to speak of this [?].

“The will is the commander of the vital force; the vital force is what fills the body. [Five illegible characters] comes next. Therefore it is said: ‘Hold fast to your will, and do not do violence to your vital force.’”
Liu Xigao.

Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: “The writer on this topic [seven illegible characters] refined [?], with fresh phrasing; his insights rise above the ordinary and are unconstrained.”

Comment by Examiner Lu, Instructor: “The expression is composed and assured; this is surely the work of someone who has thought deeply and attained insight.” 〔The expression is composed and assured; this is surely the work of someone who has thought deeply and attained insight.〕

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正丘　批　脫去冗俗
大賢推言志氣之分而皆不可以失其養也夫
志主之氣承之固定分也然則兼所重矣而養
之可以偏廢哉孟子荅公孫丑之問若謂告子
所謂不得于心勿求于氣者是徒有見于心無
見于氣也謂之可者未極言之耳要其極則氣
之在人豈其可輕者耶且人之有志所以決吾
心之趨而制天下之動者也然而斡運之效其
===
能酬酢之通其變固曰氣之作用而非志之發
縱不可也是作其氣而使之有所爲者志主之
也志非氣之帥乎人之有氣所以爲成形之具
而鼓一身之動者也故夫耳目之善其官手足
之舉其力雖曰體之良能而非氣之貫通不可
也是浹於膚而俾之無所虧者氣運之也氣非
體之充乎夫志爲氣帥則人之所以妙經綸之
功以參天地之大者於是乎在尊於一身莫得
而加矣是志固爲至焉氣爲體充則人之所以
punctuated:
考試官學正丘批：脫去冗俗。

大賢推言志氣之分，而皆不可以失其養也。夫志主之，氣承之，固定分也。然則兼所重矣，而養之可以偏廢哉？孟子荅公孫丑之問，若謂告子所謂不得于心勿求于氣者，是徒有見于心，無見于氣也。謂之可者，未極言之耳。要其極，則氣之在人，豈其可輕者耶？且人之有志，所以決吾心之趨，而制天下之動者也。然而斡運之效其能，酬酢之通其變，固曰氣之作用，而非志之發縱不可也。是作其氣而使之有所爲者，志主之也。志非氣之帥乎？人之有氣，所以爲成形之具，而鼓一身之動者也。故夫耳目之善其官，手足之舉其力，雖曰體之良能，而非氣之貫通不可也。是浹於膚而俾之無所虧者，氣運之也。氣非體之充乎？夫志爲氣帥，則人之所以妙經綸之功，以參天地之大者，於是乎在，尊於一身，莫得而加矣。是志固爲至焉。氣爲體充，則人之所以
translation_en:
Examiner Qiu, School Instructor, comments: “Free of prolixity and conventional vulgarity.”

The great worthy elaborates on the distinction between the will and vital energy (qi), showing that neither may be left unnourished. The will commands, and vital energy obeys: these are indeed their established roles. Yet both are to be valued; can either therefore be neglected in nourishing them? In answering Gongsun Chou’s question, Mencius seems to suggest that Gaozi’s statement, “What you do not obtain in the heart, do not seek in vital energy,” shows an understanding of the heart alone, without an understanding of vital energy. In calling this acceptable, Mencius merely had not pursued his explanation to its fullest extent. If we follow it to its ultimate implications, how could vital energy in a person be treated lightly?

Now, a person possesses a will in order to determine the direction of the heart and govern the movements of all under Heaven. Yet the exercise of abilities in managing affairs and the accommodation of changing circumstances in responding to things, though indeed functions of vital energy, are impossible without the will’s initiating direction. Thus, what rouses vital energy and gives it something to accomplish is the will commanding it. Is not the will the commander of vital energy?

A person possesses vital energy as the means by which bodily form is constituted and the movements of the whole body are set in motion. Thus, the ears and eyes performing their offices well and the hands and feet exerting their strength, though described as the body’s innate capacities, are impossible without vital energy coursing through them. Thus, what permeates the skin and ensures that nothing is lacking is vital energy circulating through it. Is not vital energy what fills the body?

Since the will is the commander of vital energy, here lies that by which a person achieves wondrous accomplishments in ordering affairs and participates in the greatness of Heaven and Earth. Within the person, nothing can surpass it in dignity. The will therefore assuredly comes foremost. Since vital energy is what fills the body, that by which a person …

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
配道義之用而塞天地之間者於是乎在比之
於心亦實相副矣是氣即爲次焉故曰人之志
不可以不持也必敬以守之而操存之念常爲
邪僻之防出之以虛明而主之爲克一知止有
定不亂於形氣之私斯可矣氣亦不可以或暴
也必安以養之而涵育之心常謹均調之節本
之以和順而培之以常直循其自然不傷於忿
戾之害斯可矣此固志氣交養之功而舉一廢
一之不可也告子偏于制心豈知此理者哉噫
===
孟子之不動心眞有道與抑不動心之理自孔
子發之其曰內省不疚夫何憂何懼不動心之
本也又曰敬以直內義以方外不動心之功也
彼波蕩風靡是固失其爲心而不顧是非恃其
力制者終亦歸於頑悍焉爾孟子防其流也而
特出知言養氣之論心學淵矣理本於孔子而
指氣爲言於義方益顯斯其所獨得者耶故曰
擴前聖所未發
易
punctuated:
配道義之用而塞天地之間者，於是乎在。比之於心，亦實相副矣，是氣即爲次焉。故曰：人之志不可以不持也，必敬以守之，而操存之念常爲邪僻之防；出之以虛明，而主之爲克一，知止有定，不亂於形氣之私，斯可矣。氣亦不可以或暴也，必安以養之，而涵育之心常謹均調之節；本之以和順，而培之以常直，循其自然，不傷於忿戾之害，斯可矣。此固志氣交養之功，而舉一廢一之不可也。告子偏于制心，豈知此理者哉？噫！孟子之不動心，眞有道與！抑不動心之理，自孔子發之。其曰：「內省不疚，夫何憂何懼？」不動心之本也。又曰：「敬以直內，義以方外。」不動心之功也。彼波蕩風靡，是固失其爲心；而不顧是非，恃其力制者，終亦歸於頑悍焉爾。孟子防其流也，而特出知言養氣之論，心學淵矣！理本於孔子，而指氣爲言，於義方益顯，斯其所獨得者耶？故曰：「擴前聖所未發。」

易
translation_en:
…what enables a person to complement the operation of the Way and righteousness and to fill the space between Heaven and Earth lies herein. Compared with the heart-mind, qi indeed serves as its counterpart; thus qi occupies the secondary position. Hence it is said: one must maintain one’s resolve. One must guard it with reverence, keeping the intention to preserve it constantly on guard against perversity and waywardness. Let it issue forth through openness and clarity, and govern it so as to achieve singleness of purpose. Know where to rest and become settled, undisturbed by the selfish impulses of bodily form and qi: this will suffice. Nor may one ever do violence to qi. One must nourish it with tranquillity, constantly attending, in one’s nurturing care, to the proper measures of balance and regulation. Root it in harmony and compliance, and cultivate it through constant uprightness, following its natural course without suffering the harm of anger and violence: this will suffice. Such is the work of nourishing resolve and qi together; one cannot uphold either while neglecting the other. Gaozi was partial to controlling the heart-mind. How could he have understood this principle? Ah! Mencius truly had a Way by which to keep his heart-mind unmoved!

Yet the principle of keeping the heart-mind unmoved was first expounded by Confucius. His saying, “If, upon examining yourself within, you find no cause for shame, what is there to worry about or fear?” states the foundation of an unmoved heart-mind. Again, “Through reverence, make the inner self upright; through righteousness, make outward conduct square” states the work required to keep the heart-mind unmoved. Those tossed about by waves and bent by the wind certainly lose what makes the heart-mind what it is. Yet those who disregard right and wrong and rely on forcibly controlling it ultimately lapse into obstinate fierceness. To guard against these tendencies, Mencius specifically advanced his teaching on understanding words and nourishing qi. How profound is this learning of the heart-mind! Its principle originated with Confucius, but by speaking specifically of qi, Mencius made still clearer the teaching that righteousness squares outward conduct. Was this his distinctive insight? Thus it is said: “He expanded upon what the earlier sages had not yet brought to light.”

Book of Changes (Yijing)

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄

張旂

漸爻具臣道上進之善聖人擬其象而善其占
也夫安其位而行其志仕進者莫善於此矣此
聖人於漸之六二而著其象占以明臣道也且
===
夫君子非無位之患而以無德爲患亦非無德
之患而以得遇爲難漸之六二柔順中正天下
之至德也而進上以漸上有九五剛健居尊天
下之大君也而下應於巳則是有諸巳者具熙
績亮工之體而及時向往以適其用獲乎上者
際顯俊登庸之會而行義達道不失其機由是
而進焉吾見建官定位而豐爵我加上膺錫命
之隆下係具瞻之望負乘不得而誚之高而不
危也因能授祿而大亨我養退有委蛇之適公
punctuated:
六二，鴻漸於磐，飲食衎衎，吉。

漸爻具臣道上進之善，聖人擬其象而善其占也。夫安其位而行其志，仕進者莫善於此矣。此聖人於漸之六二而著其象占，以明臣道也。且夫君子非無位之患，而以無德爲患；亦非無德之患，而以得遇爲難。漸之六二，柔順中正，天下之至德也，而進上以漸；上有九五，剛健居尊，天下之大君也，而下應於巳。則是有諸巳者，具熙績亮工之體，而及時向往以適其用；獲乎上者，際顯俊登庸之會，而行義達道不失其機。由是而進焉，吾見建官定位，而豐爵我加，上膺錫命之隆，下係具瞻之望，負乘不得而誚之，高而不危也。因能授祿，而大亨我養，退有委蛇之適，公…

Six in the second place: The wild goose gradually advances to a great rock. It eats and drinks in contentment. Auspicious.
Zhang Qi.
Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor, comments: 〔The line’s import—centrality, correctness, and a corresponding line—has been elucidated almost exhaustively. Here is someone with whom one may discuss the Book of Changes.〕
Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: 〔Clear in principle and fluent in expression.〕
Examiner Qiu, Director of Studies, comments: 〔The wording is economical, yet the meaning is complete.〕
This line of Gradual Progress embodies the excellence of advancement in the way of a minister. The sage represents it through an image and pronounces its divination auspicious. To be secure in one’s position and put one’s aspirations into practice: for those advancing in official service, nothing is better than this. Thus, for the six in the second place of Gradual Progress, the sage sets forth its image and divination to illuminate the way of a minister.
Now the gentleman worries not about lacking a position, but about lacking virtue. Nor is lacking virtue his only concern: he also regards finding a receptive ruler as difficult. The six in the second place of Gradual Progress is yielding and compliant, central and correct—the highest virtue under Heaven—and advances upward gradually. Above it is the nine in the fifth place, strong and vigorous and occupying the honored position—the great sovereign of all under Heaven—which responds downward to it. Thus, what one possesses within oneself provides the foundation for splendid achievements and the successful discharge of duties; one advances at the proper time to put these capacities to use. Gaining favor above, one encounters an occasion when the worthy are brought to prominence and appointed to office; one practices righteousness and gives effect to the Way without missing the opportunity.
Advancing in this manner, I see offices established and positions assigned, with exalted rank conferred upon me. Above, I receive the distinction of an imperial appointment; below, I bear the hopes of all who look up to me. No one can reproach me as a burden-bearer riding in a carriage: my position is high, yet free from peril. Emoluments are granted according to ability, and ample provision sustains me. In retirement from official duties, there is the ease of unhurried composure; in public service…

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
無覆餗之懼食浮不得而議之受而不愧也其
象遵渚之鴻漸于大石飲啄自如氣象衎衎者
乎占而有此吾見道因時顯脩之於家者施於
天子之庭利用大作而功在社稷由是朱紱方
來固將長守其貴於不替矣行以位成蘊之爲
德者發爲事業之大底綏四方而澤潤生民由
是天寵玆承固將長享其富於無窮矣何其吉
也是則往而有功本諸有德而成諸有應君臣
之際固君子之盛遇也周公著於漸之六二以
===
善臣道其有嘉於此與大抵德也時也有應也
三者備而後漸道全匪聖人孰能明之孰能行
之是故三聘至而伊尹興後車載而呂望出有
應而進斯爲有德保衡弼成之勳所由致也下
若壯趾浚恒冥升摧晉者亦復紛紛然則漸磐
之鴻得象寡矣是故周公著之爲臣道法也
六爻相雜唯其時物也
周宇
同考試官教諭廖　批　塲中發揮時物多欠分明此作
punctuated:
無覆餗之懼，食浮不得而議之，受而不愧也。其象遵渚之鴻，漸于大石，飲啄自如，氣象衎衎者乎？占而有此，吾見道因時顯，脩之於家者施於天子之庭，利用大作而功在社稷。由是朱紱方來，固將長守其貴於不替矣。行以位成，蘊之爲德者發爲事業之大，底綏四方而澤潤生民。由是天寵玆承，固將長享其富於無窮矣。何其吉也！是則往而有功，本諸有德，而成諸有應。君臣之際，固君子之盛遇也。周公著於漸之六二，以善臣道，其有嘉於此與？大抵德也、時也、有應也，三者備而後漸道全。匪聖人孰能明之？孰能行之？是故三聘至而伊尹興，後車載而呂望出，有應而進，斯爲有德，保衡弼成之勳所由致也。下若壯趾、浚恒、冥升、摧晉者，亦復紛紛。然則漸磐之鴻，得象寡矣。是故周公著之，爲臣道法也。
六爻相雜，唯其時物也。
周宇

translation_en:
…there is no fear of overturning the cauldron’s contents—that is, failing in office. No one can criticize his emoluments as exceeding his merits; he receives them without shame. Is his image not that of a wild goose following the islet’s edge, gradually advancing onto a great rock, drinking and pecking at ease, its bearing joyful and contented? When this is obtained in divination, I see the Way becoming manifest as the time permits: what he has cultivated at home is put into practice at the Son of Heaven’s court. It is favorable to undertake great works, and his achievements benefit the altars of soil and grain. Thus the vermilion knee-covering of rank comes to him, and he will surely preserve his noble standing long without decline. His conduct finds fulfillment through his position; what he has stored within as virtue emerges in great undertakings, bringing peace to the four quarters and extending beneficence to the people. Thus receiving Heaven’s favor, he will surely enjoy his wealth enduringly and without limit. How auspicious!
Success in going forward is therefore rooted in possessing virtue and brought to completion by having a corresponding response above. Such a meeting of ruler and minister is indeed a gentleman’s splendid opportunity. In his statement on the second, yin line of Gradual Progress, the Duke of Zhou set this forth to perfect the minister’s way. Was this not what he commended? In general, virtue, the right time, and a corresponding response must all be present before the way of gradual progress is complete. Who but a sage can understand it? Who can put it into practice? Thus Yi Yin rose when the three invitations arrived, and Lü Wang came forth when he was carried in the accompanying carriage. To advance when there is a corresponding response is conduct befitting one possessed of virtue; this was how their achievements as guardian and as helper in completing the royal enterprise came about. Below them, those who display ‘strength in the toes,’ ‘seek constancy too deeply,’ ‘ascend in darkness,’ or find their ‘advance checked’ are numerous indeed. Few, then, embody the image of the wild goose gradually advancing onto the rock. Hence the Duke of Zhou recorded it as a model for the minister’s way.
The six lines intermingle according to their times and the things they represent.
Zhou Yu

===

以方體求發揮於内外之間奇或間偶偶或間

大傳論易爻之迭用，一陰陽之適值者也。蓋時也者，陰陽所乘之運也。然則六爻之所以迭用者，夫豈有外于此哉？昔吾夫子大傳，意謂易之原始要終，卦固所以爲質矣。然則爻之所以爲義，何如耶？是故奇而實者，陽爻也。以陽居陽，固定分矣，然而非可專也。陽居之，而陰亦居之，不可以典要拘。偶而虛者，陰爻也。以陰處陰，亦常理矣，然而非有恒也。陰處之，而陽亦處之，不可以方體求。發揮於内外之間，奇或間偶，偶或間奇，紛然其交著也。變易於貞悔之内，剛或錯柔，柔或錯剛，雜然其不齊也。夫爻之所以爲爻如此，豈有他哉？蓋陰陽之具體者，物也；變化之靡常者，時也。以具體之物而趨靡常之時，卦一成質，爻亦隨之以定位矣。六位有恒而待虛也，二體無端而流布也。以虛待之，宅而棲流布之體
translation_en:
…achieves this.

Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: 〔This shows a profound understanding of the Changes and should be recorded as a model.〕

Examiner Qiu, School Instructor, comments: 〔It grasps the purport of purity, subtlety, and precision.〕

The Great Commentary discusses the alternating functions of the lines of the Changes: these depend entirely upon yin and yang encountering their appropriate circumstances. For time is the course upon which yin and yang ride. How, then, could the alternating functions of the six lines fall outside this? In the Great Commentary, our Master meant that, in tracing beginnings and comprehending endings through the Changes, the hexagram provides the underlying structure. How, then, do the lines convey meaning?

Thus, a single, solid stroke is a yang line. For yang to occupy a yang position is indeed its assigned place, yet it cannot possess that position exclusively. Yang occupies it, but yin also occupies it: this cannot be confined within fixed rules. A paired stroke with an opening is a yin line. For yin to occupy a yin position is likewise the regular principle, yet this is not invariable. Yin occupies it, but yang also occupies it: this cannot be sought in a fixed form. As they unfold between the inner and outer trigrams, single strokes sometimes alternate with paired strokes, and paired strokes sometimes alternate with single strokes; profusely they appear interwoven. As they change within the lower and upper trigrams, the firm sometimes intermingles with the yielding, and the yielding sometimes intermingles with the firm; in their diversity they are unevenly arrayed. Such is what makes the lines what they are. Could there be any other explanation?

Things are the concrete embodiments of yin and yang; time is their ceaselessly varying transformation. Concrete things move in accordance with inconstant time. Once a hexagram has taken shape, its lines accordingly assume their positions. The six positions are constant and await occupation in their emptiness; the two forms, yin and yang, circulate without end. Through their emptiness, the positions await them, lodging and housing the circulating forms…
