休
punctuated:
卦有變通，爻亦以之而定名矣。客形於二物，時乎陽也而陽趨之，時乎陰也而陰趨之。承乘比應之間，而陰陽相錯之，反復顚所遇也。否則其機息矣，何以相禪於無窮哉？旅次於六位，時乎六也而六主之，時乎九也而九主之。貴賤遠近之地，而九六迭處之，交互唯所適也。否則其化滯矣，何以引伸於不已哉？是知相雜者其數也，趨時者其理也。數無止極，而理無盡藏，此爻之可以至數萬而天下之能事畢也。抑論時之義，大矣哉！天不能違，故寒暑運；物不能違，故代謝彰。天地之所以不已，物生之所以不窮，職此故也。聖人取而著之於易，然後道化泄而人事盡。善體之，則天命物理斡旋之機在我矣。萬物不能逃陰陽，陰陽不能違其時，易深矣乎！論者曰：「說天者莫辯乎易。」足之曰：「說易者莫辯乎時。」
書
惟動丕應徯志，以昭受上帝，天其申命用休。
translation_en:
…As the hexagrams change and adapt, their lines likewise receive their designations accordingly. Taking temporary form in the two entities, yin and yang, they tend toward yang when the time calls for yang, and toward yin when the time calls for yin. In the relationships of supporting, riding upon, adjacency, and correspondence, yin and yang intermingle, reversing and overturning according to what they encounter [?]. Otherwise, their mechanism would cease: how could they succeed one another without end? Lodging temporarily in the six positions, they are governed by six when the time calls for six, and by nine when the time calls for nine. In places high and low, near and far, nines and sixes take turns residing, interchanging according to where they fit. Otherwise, their transformations would stagnate: how could they extend and develop unceasingly?
Thus we know that intermingling belongs to their numerical configurations, while responding to the time belongs to their underlying principle. Their numerical configurations have no limit, and their principle is an inexhaustible store. This is why the lines can reach tens of thousands in number and encompass all that can be accomplished under Heaven. Indeed, how great is the significance of timeliness! Heaven cannot depart from it, and so cold and heat revolve; things cannot depart from it, and so succession and decline become manifest. This alone explains why Heaven and Earth never cease and why the generation of things is inexhaustible. The sages took this and set it forth in the Book of Changes; only then were the transformations of the Way revealed and human affairs fully comprehended. If we embody it well, the mechanism governing the workings of Heaven’s mandate and the principles of things lies within us. The myriad things cannot escape yin and yang, and yin and yang cannot depart from their proper times. How profound is the Book of Changes! A commentator said: “Nothing explains Heaven more clearly than the Book of Changes.” I would supplement this by saying: “Nothing explains the Book of Changes more clearly than timeliness.”
Book of Documents
“In all your actions, respond fully to the aspirations of those who await their fulfillment, thereby gloriously receiving the favor of the Lord on High; Heaven will then renew its mandate with blessings.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
楊吉
天人感應之妙在徯志中命是
同考試官教諭魏　批
作聞揚得出明經士也取之
考試官教諭盧　批
辭典雅而意精到
考試官學正丘　批
氣渾語潔可式
大臣舉天人協應之妙所以廣慎位之意也夫
君心天人之會也苟愼位而交脩焉天人之妙
應也固其理哉大禹陳愼位之謨于舜復推其
意如此蓋曰人君之御天下也愼位以爲本交
===
脩以爲功允若茲夫豈無其應耶是故民罔常
懷其心未易得也夫惟其交脩也則明明之后
德既允協乎人心而有所敷也有所爲也自潛
孚乎衆志吾見言莫不信罔越厥志矣而媚茲
之誠若將徯其所欲爲焉行莫不悅咸一乃心
矣而孚感之速殆有先于其所動焉所謂不言
而信不令而行者是矣民能外君以爲心乎天
難諶斯其命不于常也夫惟其交脩也則遲遲
之昭假既克享乎天心而受于上也膺于下也
punctuated:
楊吉

天人感應之妙，在徯志中，命是。
同考試官教諭魏批。

作聞揚得出，明經士也，取之。
考試官教諭盧批。

辭典雅而意精到。
考試官學正丘批。

氣渾語潔，可式。

大臣舉天人協應之妙，所以廣慎位之意也。夫君心，天人之會也。苟愼位而交脩焉，天人之妙應也，固其理哉！大禹陳愼位之謨于舜，復推其意如此，蓋曰：人君之御天下也，愼位以爲本，交脩以爲功。允若茲，夫豈無其應耶？是故民罔常懷，其心未易得也。夫惟其交脩也，則明明之后，德既允協乎人心，而有所敷也，有所爲也，自潛孚乎衆志。吾見言莫不信，罔越厥志矣，而媚茲之誠，若將徯其所欲爲焉；行莫不悅，咸一乃心矣，而孚感之速，殆有先于其所動焉。所謂不言而信，不令而行者，是矣。民能外君以爲心乎？天難諶斯，其命不于常也。夫惟其交脩也，則遲遲之昭假，既克享乎天心，而受于上也，膺于下也，
translation_en:
Yang Ji

“The subtle workings of the sympathetic response between Heaven and humanity lie in ‘awaiting his intentions’; ‘mandate—this’ [?].”
Comment by Associate Examiner Wei, Instructor.

“The composition brings out and develops what has been heard [?]. He is a scholar versed in the Classics. Accept him.”
Comment by Examiner Lu, Instructor.

“The diction is classically elegant, and the thought precise and thorough.”
Comment by Examiner Qiu, School Instructor.

“The expressive force is full and integrated, the language concise; it can serve as a model.”

The great minister sets forth the subtle workings of the harmonious response between Heaven and humanity in order to expand upon the meaning of being mindful of one’s position. The ruler’s heart is where Heaven and humanity meet. If he is mindful of his position and cultivates himself in both respects, then surely the wondrous response of Heaven and humanity follows as a matter of principle! The Great Yu presented to Shun his counsel on being mindful of one’s position, and further developed its meaning in this way. His meaning was this: when a ruler governs all under Heaven, mindfulness of his position is the foundation, and cultivation in both respects is the work to be accomplished. If he truly acts thus, how could there be no response?

Thus, the people have no constant attachment; their hearts are not easily won. Yet through this cultivation in both respects, the virtue of the enlightened ruler truly accords with the people’s hearts. Whatever he promulgates and whatever he undertakes naturally and imperceptibly wins the trust of the multitude. I see that none distrust his words, which never depart from their aspirations; in their sincere love for him, they seem to await whatever he wishes to do. None are displeased by his actions, and all unite their hearts with his; so swiftly does this response of trust arise that it almost precedes his action. This is what is meant by being trusted without speaking and having things carried out without issuing orders. Can the people form intentions apart from their ruler?

Heaven is difficult to rely upon, and its mandate does not remain constant. Yet through this cultivation in both respects, his enduring sincerity reaches on high [?] and wins acceptance in Heaven’s heart. What he receives from above and accepts here below …

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
靡不靈承乎帝眷吾見貴爲天子純佑命矣而
多益之俾申錫無疆焉富有四海綏其祿矣而
滋至之休有隆無替焉所謂惟日不足以莫不
增者是矣天能外君以爲命乎吁觀于天人相
與之際而內外交脩之功可弗至與愼乃在位
帝其念哉抑嘗論之帝德如舜不可尚已而愼
位之儆禹復拳拳于告君者豈曰過計矣乎葢
憂治世而戒無虞大臣愛君無已之心勑天命
而謹時幾周虞廷之心法也他日愼乃有位之
訓舜亦以命于禹矣天祿永終之戒又非堯之
所以授舜乎故曰三聖相授守一道
===
文王惟克厥宅心乃克立茲常事司牧人
以克俊有德
周之頔
同考試官教諭魏 批〔知人而孚其心是文王得人之本此作能發之宜錄以式〕
考試官教諭盧 批〔文思精練優於衆作〕
考試官學正丘 批〔平通〕
punctuated:
靡不靈承乎帝眷。吾見貴爲天子，純佑命矣，而多益之，俾申錫無疆焉；富有四海，綏其祿矣，而滋至之休，有隆無替焉。所謂惟日不足以莫不增者是矣。天能外君以爲命乎？吁！觀于天人相與之際，而內外交脩之功可弗至與？愼乃在位，帝其念哉！抑嘗論之，帝德如舜，不可尚已，而愼位之儆，禹復拳拳于告君者，豈曰過計矣乎？葢憂治世而戒無虞，大臣愛君無已之心；勑天命而謹時幾，周虞廷之心法也。他日「愼乃有位」之訓，舜亦以命于禹矣。「天祿永終」之戒，又非堯之所以授舜乎？故曰：三聖相授，守一道。

文王惟克厥宅心，乃克立茲常事司牧人，以克俊有德。
周之頔
同考試官教諭魏，批〔知人而孚其心，是文王得人之本。此作能發之，宜錄以式。〕
考試官教諭盧，批〔文思精練，優於衆作。〕
考試官學正丘，批〔平通。〕
translation_en:
…all fittingly receive the favor of the Lord on High. I see the ruler, exalted as the Son of Heaven, receiving Heaven’s full protection and mandate; these are further increased, so that blessings are bestowed upon him repeatedly and without limit. Possessing the wealth of all within the Four Seas, he is secure in his heavenly bounty; blessings arrive in increasing abundance, ever growing and never declining. This is what is meant by saying that the days scarcely suffice for all that continually increases. Can Heaven determine its mandate apart from the ruler? Ah! Observing the interplay between Heaven and humanity, can one fail to perfect the work of cultivating both inner virtue and outward conduct? Be vigilant in your position: may the emperor bear this in mind!

Yet I have reflected on this: imperial virtue such as Shun’s could not be surpassed, but Yu still earnestly admonished his sovereign to be vigilant in his position. Could this be called excessive caution? To remain concerned in an age of good government and exercise vigilance when there is no apparent cause for anxiety expresses the great minister’s unceasing love for his ruler. To attend reverently to Heaven’s mandate and carefully watch the incipient signs of events was the essential teaching of the courts of Zhou and Yu [?]. Later, Shun himself charged Yu with the instruction, “Be vigilant in the position you occupy.” And was not the warning, “Heaven’s bounty will end forever,” also what Yao transmitted to Shun? Thus it is said: the three sages handed down their charge to one another, holding fast to a single Way.

“King Wen could discern where their hearts rested; thus he could establish these standing officers, directors of affairs, and shepherds of the people, employing outstanding men of virtue.”

Zhou Zhiqi.

Associate Examiner Wei, Instructor, comments: “To understand men and win their hearts was the foundation of King Wen’s success in obtaining worthy men. This composition brings that out and should be recorded as a model.”

Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: “The thought and expression are refined and concise, superior to the other compositions.”

Examiner Qiu, Instructor, comments: “Even and coherent.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
前王于三宅惟能得其心斯能得其用焉夫知
人者官人之本也前王能得三宅之心則能得
斯人以爲用也宜哉周公進戒成王及此謂夫
立政以擇長爲要用人以知人爲先我周得人
之盛文王固有道矣文王之于三宅不惟稽之
於貌也視所以而察所安蓋巳得其隱微之奥
不徒謀之於面也精與契而神與合蓋巳略其
形迹之粗才何所宜德何可用知之不爽若懸
諸藻鑑而纖悉畢照也三宅之有心乎文王之
===
心矣德可懋官言可底績相得而章殆亮其衷
悰而羣疑俱亡也文王之爲心以三宅之心矣
夫旣克厥宅心則豈不能立兹宅俊乎蓋知之
至則心不眩而取舍之極定信之篤則心不貳
而委任之志專是以立之爲常事者必其經綸
內蘊足以成天下之務而贊帝載於咸熈立之
爲司牧者必其豈弟中涵足以立天下之愛而
奠民生於丕冒卽宅卽俊卓乎王國之楨表儀
朝著者固以馮以翼者也位之浮於德者何有
punctuated: 前王于三宅，惟能得其心，斯能得其用焉。夫知人者，官人之本也。前王能得三宅之心，則能得斯人以爲用也，宜哉！周公進戒成王及此，謂夫立政以擇長爲要，用人以知人爲先，我周得人之盛，文王固有道矣。文王之于三宅，不惟稽之於貌也，視所以而察所安，蓋巳得其隱微之奥；不徒謀之於面也，精與契而神與合，蓋巳略其形迹之粗。才何所宜，德何可用，知之不爽，若懸諸藻鑑而纖悉畢照也。三宅之有心乎，文王之心矣。德可懋官，言可底績，相得而章，殆亮其衷悰而羣疑俱亡也。文王之爲心，以三宅之心矣。夫旣克厥宅心，則豈不能立兹宅俊乎？蓋知之至則心不眩，而取舍之極定；信之篤則心不貳，而委任之志專。是以立之爲常事者，必其經綸內蘊，足以成天下之務，而贊帝載於咸熈；立之爲司牧者，必其豈弟中涵，足以立天下之愛，而奠民生於丕冒。卽宅卽俊，卓乎王國之楨，表儀朝著者，固以馮以翼者也。位之浮於德者，何有
translation_en:
Only by winning the hearts of those occupying the three classes of office could the former king secure their service. Understanding men is the foundation of appointing them to office. Since the former king could win the hearts of those in the three classes of office, it was fitting that he should obtain their service. The Duke of Zhou reached this point in presenting his admonition to King Cheng: establishing government depends above all on choosing its leaders, and employing men requires first understanding them. King Wen certainly had a method by which our Zhou obtained so abundant a company of worthy men.

In dealing with those in the three classes of office, King Wen did not judge them merely by their appearance. He observed how they acted and examined what put their minds at ease, thereby grasping the deepest recesses of their hidden thoughts. Nor did he merely consult them face to face: their inner essences accorded and their spirits met, so that he had already passed beyond the outward traces of conduct. What tasks their talents suited them for, and what service their virtue fitted them to render—he understood these without error, as though setting them before a discerning mirror in which every minute detail was illuminated. The hearts of those in the three classes of office were King Wen’s own heart. Their virtue could enhance their offices, and their words could be realized in accomplishments. Ruler and ministers complemented one another and brought each other’s qualities to light; he understood their innermost feelings, and every doubt disappeared. King Wen took the hearts of those in the three classes of office as his own.

Having thus understood the hearts of those he appointed, how could he fail to establish worthy men in these offices? When understanding is complete, the mind is free from confusion, and the standard for accepting or rejecting men is settled. When trust is firm, the mind is undivided, and the resolve to entrust responsibility is steadfast. Thus, those he appointed to manage regular affairs necessarily possessed an inward capacity for ordering the world, sufficient to accomplish its business and help bring the sovereign’s undertakings to universal prosperity. Those he appointed as governors of the people necessarily possessed an inward gentleness and kindness, sufficient to establish love throughout the world and secure the people’s livelihood under far-reaching protection. Whoever occupied an office was worthy: outstanding pillars of the royal realm, serving as models at court, they were indeed men on whom he could rely and who could assist him. How could there be anyone whose rank exceeded his virtue …

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
耶義德容德允矣邦家之基潤澤生民者固令
聞令望者也實不稱其名者何有耶由是官長
賢矣而擇屬宜無不賢我周所以得人之盛者
職此耳文王知恤之實於此昭然矣抑知恤之
說原於虞廷臯陶曰在知人禹曰惟帝其難之
又曰知人則哲能官人垂萬世用人之法也而
夏而商迪知忱恂嚴惟丕式惟是之宗耳周公
言文武之知恤而舉夏商爲言即其近而承者
乎嗚呼自唐虞夏商以及有周皆以知人爲恤
後世又可推矣惜乎猶爲知恤之鮮也然則宜
知何孔子告哀公曰取人以身脩身以道揭其
本矣
===
詩
吉甫燕喜既多受祉來歸自鎬我行永久
飲御諸友炰鱉膾鯉侯誰在矣張仲孝
友
王希堯
同考試官教諭熊　批〔詩旨重燕喜是作意格融貫〕
punctuated:
耶？義德容德，允矣邦家之基；潤澤生民者，固令聞令望者也，實不稱其名者何有耶？由是官長賢矣，而擇屬宜無不賢。我周所以得人之盛者，職此耳。文王知恤之實，於此昭然矣。抑知恤之說，原於虞廷。臯陶曰：「在知人。」禹曰：「惟帝其難之。」又曰：「知人則哲，能官人。」垂萬世用人之法也。而夏而商，迪知忱恂，嚴惟丕式，惟是之宗耳。周公言文武之知恤，而舉夏商爲言，即其近而承者乎？嗚呼！自唐虞夏商以及有周，皆以知人爲恤，後世又可推矣。惜乎猶爲知恤之鮮也！然則宜知何？孔子告哀公曰：「取人以身，脩身以道。」揭其本矣。

詩
吉甫燕喜，既多受祉。來歸自鎬，我行永久。飲御諸友，炰鱉膾鯉。侯誰在矣？張仲孝友。
王希堯
同考試官教諭熊，批〔詩旨重燕喜，是作意格融貫〕
translation_en:
…could there be any? Those righteous and capacious in virtue are indeed the foundations of the state; those who confer benefits upon the people surely possess a fine reputation and high esteem. How could there be any whose substance failed to match their name? Thus the heads of offices were worthy, and all the subordinates they selected should likewise have been worthy. This alone accounts for the abundance of talented men secured by our Zhou. Here King Wen’s actual understanding of what deserved his concern becomes manifest.

Yet the teaching about knowing what deserves concern originated at the court of Shun. Gao Yao said, “It lies in knowing men.” Yu said, “Even the emperor finds this difficult.” He also said, “Knowing men constitutes wisdom: thus one can appoint men to office.” These words handed down a rule for employing men for all ages. Under Xia and Shang, they followed this understanding with sincerity and trust, reverently taking it as their great model; this alone was their guiding principle. When the Duke of Zhou spoke of Kings Wen and Wu’s understanding of what deserved concern and cited Xia and Shang, was it because these were the nearby precedents they inherited? Alas! From Tang and Yu through Xia and Shang down to Zhou, all made knowing men their concern; the same principle may be extended to later ages. Regrettably, those who know what deserves concern are still few! What, then, should one know? Confucius told Duke Ai, “Select men by taking your own person as the measure; cultivate your person through the Way.” He thereby disclosed the root of the matter.

Book of Odes

Jifu rejoices at the feast,
Having received abundant blessings.
Returning from Hao,
I have been long upon the road.
I entertain my friends with drink,
With roasted turtles and sliced raw carp.
Who is present there?
Zhang Zhong, filial and devoted to his brothers.

By Wang Xiyao.

Associate Examiner Xiong, Instructor, comments: 〔The purport of the ode centers on joy at the feast. In this composition, conception and form are thoroughly integrated…〕

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
采爛然故錄之
同考試官教授馬　批〔模寫凱還燕樂之意宛然在目〕
考試官教諭盧　批〔氣昌詞達〕
考試官學正丘　批〔純正〕
詩人原大將燕飲之慶因賢其與燕者以美之
也夫歸遠行久凱旋之慶也燕喜而孝友之賢
與焉豈不足以益重斯燕哉宜詩人之善之也
昔周尹吉甫伐玁狁有功而歸詩人敘其事以
美之蓋曰我吉甫也太原之師既捷玁狁之難
===
于襄其旋師也獨無可言者乎吾見其國難夷
而兵權釋雍雍于罇俎之陳純嘏其時斂矣膚
功奏而王心寧衎衎于燕樂之需多福其聿懷
矣是蓋敵王愾以爲功安社稷以爲福也受祉
不既多耶然是燕也問其來則爰歸自鎬旅而
即安寧無陶然于中矣乎問其時則嗣續我日
渙而復萃寧無暢然于懷矣乎茲燕之不可已
也由是進厥諸友酒以飲之而奠獻酬酢之禮
行洽彼朋好肴以將之而炰鼈膾鯉之羞備然
punctuated:
采爛然，故錄之。
同考試官教授馬批〔模寫凱還燕樂之意，宛然在目〕
考試官教諭盧批〔氣昌詞達〕
考試官學正丘批〔純正〕
詩人原大將燕飲之慶，因賢其與燕者以美之也。夫歸遠行久，凱旋之慶也；燕喜而孝友之賢與焉，豈不足以益重斯燕哉？宜詩人之善之也。
昔周尹吉甫伐玁狁有功而歸，詩人敘其事以美之。蓋曰：我吉甫也，太原之師既捷，玁狁之難于襄，其旋師也，獨無可言者乎？吾見其國難夷而兵權釋，雍雍于罇俎之陳，純嘏其時斂矣；膚功奏而王心寧，衎衎于燕樂之需，多福其聿懷矣。是蓋敵王愾以爲功，安社稷以爲福也，受祉不既多耶？然是燕也，問其來，則爰歸自鎬，旅而即安，寧無陶然于中矣乎？問其時，則嗣續我日，渙而復萃，寧無暢然于懷矣乎？茲燕之不可已也。由是進厥諸友，酒以飲之，而奠獻酬酢之禮行；洽彼朋好，肴以將之，而炰鼈膾鯉之羞備。然……
translation_en:
…its literary brilliance shines forth; therefore I have selected it for inclusion.
Associate Examiner Ma, Professor, comments: 〔The depiction of the triumphant return and the pleasures of the feast makes the scene seem vividly present before one’s eyes.〕
Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: 〔Abundant vigor and fluent expression.〕
Examiner Qiu, Instructor, comments: 〔Pure and correct.〕
The poet traces the reasons for the great general’s celebratory feast and praises it on account of the worthiness of those who attended. Returning from afar after a lengthy campaign was an occasion to celebrate victory. When worthy men distinguished by filial devotion and brotherly affection joined the joyful feast, was this not sufficient to lend it still greater importance? It was fitting that the poet should commend it.
In former times, Yin Jifu of Zhou returned after successfully campaigning against the Xianyun, and the poet recounted his deeds in praise. The meaning is this: Our Jifu had won victory in the campaign at Taiyuan, and the trouble caused by the Xianyun had been removed. Could there be nothing worth recounting about his army’s return? I see that, with the danger to the state quelled and his military authority relinquished, he sits harmoniously among the arrayed wine vessels and serving stands: great blessings are now gathered to him. With his great achievement accomplished and the king’s heart at peace, he delights in the provisions for the feast: manifold blessings now come to him. His achievement lay in confronting those who aroused the king’s anger; his blessing lay in securing the altars of soil and grain. Had he not received blessings in abundance?
As for this feast, if one asks whence he came, he had returned from Hao. Having traveled and now reached repose, could he fail to feel inward delight? If one asks about its timing, his days had stretched on and on [?]; after dispersal came reunion. Could he fail to feel joy in his heart? This was why the feast could not be omitted. Accordingly, he invited his friends forward and gave them wine to drink, performing the rites of setting out offerings, presenting wine, and exchanging cups. He showed affection for his good friends and served them dishes, providing delicacies of roasted turtle and sliced raw carp. Yet…

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
豈伊異人哉時則有若張仲之賢克敦孝友之
實順德之行允一國之良也令德之譽錫初筵
之光也則夫同心之比同氣之求固其所必至
者矣斯燕也不亦善乎卽是而觀則知凱旋之
樂非游佚也功之所以宣嘉會之賢非私昵也
德之所以就吉甫得友以成德宣王得臣以成
功功以德立德以助成其旣也君以臣明友道
也臣道也君道也是詩備焉中興之盛有由然
矣詩人之善于序功者如是厥後祈父歌興履
霜操作則宣王之所以得臣吉甫之所以資友
者毋亦有遺憾與噫
===
赫赫厥聲濯濯厥靈壽考且寧以保我後
生
王制
同考試官敎諭熊 批〔赫赫濯濯四字講者多欠分曉此作足以發之〕
同考試官敎授馬 批〔語意精到結尤雋永〕
考試官敎諭盧 批〔典則可誦〕
punctuated:
豈伊異人哉？時則有若張仲之賢，克敦孝友之實，順德之行，允一國之良也；令德之譽，錫初筵之光也。則夫同心之比、同氣之求，固其所必至者矣。斯燕也，不亦善乎？卽是而觀，則知凱旋之樂非游佚也，功之所以宣；嘉會之賢非私昵也，德之所以就。吉甫得友以成德，宣王得臣以成功。功以德立，德以助成，其旣也，君以臣明。友道也，臣道也，君道也，是詩備焉。中興之盛，有由然矣。詩人之善于序功者如是。厥後《祈父》歌興，《履霜》操作，則宣王之所以得臣、吉甫之所以資友者，毋亦有遺憾與？噫！

赫赫厥聲，濯濯厥靈，壽考且寧，以保我後生。
王制

同考試官敎諭熊批〔赫赫濯濯四字講者多欠分曉此作足以發之〕
同考試官敎授馬批〔語意精到結尤雋永〕
考試官敎諭盧批〔典則可誦〕
translation_en:
…Could these have been strangers? Among them at that time was the worthy Zhang Zhong, who earnestly practiced filial devotion and brotherly affection. His conduct accorded with virtue: truly he was an outstanding man of the state. His reputation for excellent virtue lent lustre to the opening of the feast. Thus the association of like-minded men and the mutual attraction of kindred spirits were assuredly bound to follow. Was this banquet not admirable? Viewed in this light, the joy of triumphant return was no idle indulgence: it was the means of proclaiming achievement. The gathering of worthy men at this splendid feast was no private favoritism: it was the means of perfecting virtue. Jifu gained friends through whom to perfect his virtue; King Xuan gained ministers through whom to accomplish his achievements. Achievement was established through virtue, and virtue brought it to completion [?]; in the end, the ruler was made illustrious through his ministers. The way of friendship, the way of ministers, and the way of rulers are all fully present in this poem. The flourishing restoration therefore had its reasons. Such was the poet’s skill in recounting achievements. Later, when the song “Minister of War” (Qifu) arose and the zither piece “Treading on Frost” (Lüshuang) was composed, might there not have remained some cause for regret concerning King Xuan’s success in obtaining ministers and Jifu’s reliance upon friends? Alas!

“Resplendent was his renown; manifest was his numinous might. Long-lived and at peace, he protected us, his descendants.”
Wang Zhi

Associate Examiner Xiong, Instructor, comments: “Those who expound the four characters he he and zhuo zhuo often fail to distinguish their meanings clearly. This composition adequately elucidates them.”
Associate Examiner Ma, Professor, comments: “The language and meaning are finely wrought and exact; the conclusion is especially rich in lingering significance.”
Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: “Classically correct and worthy of recitation.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正丘　批〔雄渾〕
詩人于前王必賛其聞望之隆而本其垂裕之
遠也夫德威所以隆聞望而久道足以裕後昆
也商人廟頌以是繹思其功至矣哉此祀高宗
之樂歌也蓋曰帝王之御世也有撥亂之功有
垂裕之澤吾于高宗徵其盛矣是故荆楚服而
多辟懼商邑建而萬國宗由是播之爲王猷也
豐功盛烈巍巍乎其有成義問休聲沛然其莫禦
一人御天下之極畿甸要荒罔非厥聲之洋溢
===
矣是何其赫赫爾耶振之爲王靈也無兢不回
丕顯日中之治不僣不濫孔昭風動之休天子
爲天下之綱中華蠻貊莫非厥靈之炳燿矣是
何其濯濯爾耶又且耆艾引其休而年所多歷
令聞旣長世矣康寧大其福而天壽平格純嘏
且爾常矣則熙洽之治永孚休于邦家有秩斯
祜我後人藉之以爲安者曷其極耶燕翼之圖
大貽謀于孫子無疆惟休我後人引之以自庇
者烏乎窮耶是知聲靈之盛自一身而沛之天
punctuated:
考試官學正丘　批〔雄渾〕

詩人于前王，必賛其聞望之隆，而本其垂裕之遠也。夫德威所以隆聞望，而久道足以裕後昆也。商人廟頌，以是繹思其功，至矣哉！此祀高宗之樂歌也。蓋曰：帝王之御世也，有撥亂之功，有垂裕之澤，吾于高宗徵其盛矣。是故荆楚服而多辟懼，商邑建而萬國宗。由是播之爲王猷也，豐功盛烈，巍巍乎其有成；義問休聲，沛然其莫禦。一人御天下之極，畿甸要荒，罔非厥聲之洋溢矣。是何其赫赫爾耶！振之爲王靈也，無兢不回，丕顯日中之治；不僣不濫，孔昭風動之休。天子爲天下之綱，中華蠻貊，莫非厥靈之炳燿矣。是何其濯濯爾耶！又且耆艾引其休，而年所多歷，令聞旣長世矣；康寧大其福，而天壽平格，純嘏且爾常矣。則熙洽之治，永孚休于邦家，有秩斯祜，我後人藉之以爲安者，曷其極耶！燕翼之圖，大貽謀于孫子，無疆惟休，我後人引之以自庇者，烏乎窮耶！是知聲靈之盛，自一身而沛之天
translation_en:
Examiner Qiu, School Instructor, comments: 〔Majestic and powerful.〕

When the poet speaks of former kings, he invariably praises the greatness of their renown and prestige, grounding it in the far-reaching bounty they bequeathed. For virtue and awe-inspiring authority magnify renown and prestige, while an enduring Way suffices to enrich later descendants. With these thoughts, the people of Shang pondered their king’s achievements in their ancestral-temple hymn. How consummate their praise! This is the ceremonial song for sacrifices to Gaozong. Its meaning is this: when emperors and kings govern the world, they accomplish the suppression of disorder and bestow benefits upon posterity. In Gaozong I find evidence of these achievements in their fullest measure. Thus Jing and Chu submitted, and the many rulers stood in fear; the Shang capital was established, and the myriad states acknowledged its supremacy. His achievements were thereby proclaimed as the king’s exemplary governance: abundant accomplishments and glorious deeds rose loftily to fulfillment; his righteous reputation and auspicious fame flowed forth irresistibly. The One Man occupied the supreme position over all under Heaven, and throughout the royal domain, the surrounding territories, and the distant frontiers, his fame overflowed everywhere. How illustrious it was!

Manifested as royal spiritual power, it admitted neither contention nor perversity [?], splendidly displaying a reign like the sun at noon; without error or excess, it brilliantly revealed the beneficent influence that moved people as the wind does. The Son of Heaven served as the guiding bond of the world, and among both the people of the central lands and the Man and Mo peoples, his spiritual power shone everywhere. How radiant it was! Moreover, in venerable old age he prolonged his excellence, living through many years, and his good name had already endured for generations. Peace and well-being enlarged his blessings, and he peacefully attained his Heaven-appointed lifespan [?]; great blessings would remain constantly his.

Thus the flourishing and harmonious government brought enduring goodness to the realm. These blessings continued in due succession: how could there be any limit to the security that we, his descendants, derived from them? His plans to shelter posterity bequeathed great counsels to his descendants, bringing boundless goodness: how could the protection that we, his descendants, drew from them ever be exhausted? From this we know that the fullness of his fame and spiritual power proceeded from his own person and poured forth throughout all under Heaven…

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
下者也垂裕之休自一世而遞之萬世者也高
宗之大造有商如此其侈之登歌也宜哉抑高
宗功德之盛固矣然致之何所自耶蓋甘盤之
學端其始夢賚之弼相其成終始典學可久之
道不敢怠遑有恒之心是故德脩罔覺而治底
中興有不已之學而後有不世之功也嗚呼惟
其有不世之功是以有不遷之祀
春秋
柔會宋公陳侯蔡叔盟于折　公會宋公
===
于夫鍾　冬十有二月公會宋公于闞
〔俱桓公十有一年〕　公會宋公于虛　冬
十有一月公會宋公于龜〔俱桓公十有
二年〕
劉希皐
同考試官教諭蔡　批〔聖人公天下之志發明殆盡宜〕
〔錄以式〕
考試官教諭盧　批〔得經意〕
考試官學正丘　批〔精確〕
punctuated:
下者也；垂裕之休，自一世而遞之萬世者也。高宗之大造有商如此，其侈之登歌也，宜哉！抑高宗功德之盛固矣，然致之何所自耶？蓋甘盤之學端其始，夢賚之弼相其成。終始典學，可久之道；不敢怠遑，有恒之心。是故德脩罔覺，而治底中興。有不已之學，而後有不世之功也。嗚呼！惟其有不世之功，是以有不遷之祀。
春秋
柔會宋公、陳侯、蔡叔盟于折。公會宋公于夫鍾。冬十有二月，公會宋公于闞。〔俱桓公十有一年〕公會宋公于虛。冬十有一月，公會宋公于龜。〔俱桓公十有二年〕
劉希皐
同考試官教諭蔡，批〔聖人公天下之志，發明殆盡，宜〕〔錄以式。〕
考試官教諭盧，批〔得經意。〕
考試官學正丘，批〔精確。〕
translation_en:
…throughout all under Heaven. The blessings of the prosperity he bequeathed pass from one age down through ten thousand ages. Such were Gaozong’s great achievements for Shang: how fitting that they should be celebrated so lavishly in the hymn sung in the ancestral hall! Gaozong’s achievements and virtue were indeed magnificent, but from what source did they arise? Instruction under Gan Pan set him on the right course at the outset; the assisting minister bestowed through a dream helped bring his work to completion. Making learning his constant concern from beginning to end was his enduring Way; never daring to lapse into idleness was his steadfast resolve. Thus his virtue developed imperceptibly, and his government brought about the dynasty’s restoration. Only through unceasing learning can there be achievements unmatched in an age. Ah! It is because his achievements were unmatched that sacrifices to him endure, his ancestral tablet never being removed.
Spring and Autumn Annals
Rou met with the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, and Shu of Cai to make a covenant at Zhe. The duke met with the Duke of Song at Fuzhong. In winter, in the twelfth month, the duke met with the Duke of Song at Kan. 〔All in the eleventh year of Duke Huan.〕 The duke met with the Duke of Song at Xu. In winter, in the eleventh month, the duke met with the Duke of Song at Gui. 〔Both in the twelfth year of Duke Huan.〕
Liu Xigao
Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: 〔“The sage’s aspiration to make all under Heaven common to all is elucidated almost completely. This should be〕〔recorded as a model.”〕
Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: 〔“Grasps the meaning of the Classic.”〕
Examiner Qiu, Instructor (xuezheng), comments: 〔“Precise and accurate.”〕

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
春秋詳紀內外之盟會而示公天下之志焉葢
大道為公盟會不足恃也魯宋之盟會有足恃
乎昔鄭宋交惡魯之與鄭也舊矣于郎有戰宋
伺其隙而通好于魯先與柔有于折之盟旣與
公有夫鍾之會又恐其好之不篤也再會于闞
于虛于龜焉斯亦盟會之常耳何備存而不削
耶葢先王以信率天下而設官以司盟實有不
得已焉者于人不足信而求信于神風已下矣
況屢盟而卒叛者乎宋之于魯欲通好于君先
===
結信于臣于心可謂誠矣何尋取伐國之師耶
言猶在耳廿蹈背盟之罪信不由衷徒為長亂
之階吾恐神不足恃將何所恃為信耶先王以
禮御天下而時會以發禁實所以懲不義者禁
不發于上而私會于下典已干矣況數會而卒
離者乎魯之于宋一會不已而至于再再會不
已而至于四于情可謂密矣何即有戰宋之舉
耶壇坫未掃而即事夫兵戈揖讓方興而即變
為仇敵吾恐禮不足恃將何所恃為敬耶聖人
punctuated: 春秋詳紀內外之盟會，而示公天下之志焉。葢大道為公，盟會不足恃也。魯宋之盟會有足恃乎？昔鄭宋交惡，魯之與鄭也舊矣。于郎有戰，宋伺其隙而通好于魯，先與柔有于折之盟，旣與公有夫鍾之會，又恐其好之不篤也，再會于闞、于虛、于龜焉。斯亦盟會之常耳，何備存而不削耶？葢先王以信率天下，而設官以司盟，實有不得已焉者。于人不足信，而求信于神，風已下矣，況屢盟而卒叛者乎？宋之于魯，欲通好于君，先結信于臣，于心可謂誠矣，何尋取伐國之師耶？言猶在耳，廿蹈背盟之罪，信不由衷，徒為長亂之階。吾恐神不足恃，將何所恃為信耶？先王以禮御天下，而時會以發禁，實所以懲不義者。禁不發于上，而私會于下，典已干矣，況數會而卒離者乎？魯之于宋，一會不已而至于再，再會不已而至于四，于情可謂密矣，何即有戰宋之舉耶？壇坫未掃，而即事夫兵戈；揖讓方興，而即變為仇敵。吾恐禮不足恃，將何所恃為敬耶？聖人
translation_en:
The Spring and Autumn Annals records in detail the covenants and meetings involving Lu and the other states, thereby revealing the Sage’s intention to make all under Heaven a common possession. For the Great Way serves the common good; covenants and meetings cannot be relied upon. Was there anything dependable in the covenants and meetings between Lu and Song? Formerly, Zheng and Song were at odds, while Lu’s association with Zheng was already longstanding. There was a battle at Lang. Song watched for an opening and established friendly relations with Lu, first making a covenant with Rou at Zhe and subsequently meeting with the duke at Fuzhong. Still fearing that their friendship was not firm, they met again at Kan, Xu, and Gui. These were merely ordinary covenants and meetings. Why preserve them all without deleting any?

The former kings led all under Heaven through trustworthiness, yet appointed officials to oversee covenants: this was truly a concession to necessity. When people could no longer be trusted and guarantees of faith had to be sought from the spirits, customs had already declined. How much worse, then, to make repeated covenants and finally betray them! In its dealings with Lu, Song wished to establish friendship with the ruler and first pledged good faith with his minister. Its intentions could be called sincere. Why, then, did it soon bring upon itself an army attacking its state? The words still rang in their ears, yet they incurred the guilt of breaking the covenant [?]. Good faith did not come from the heart; it merely became a stepping stone to greater disorder. I fear that the spirits cannot be relied upon. What, then, can be relied upon to secure good faith?

The former kings governed all under Heaven through ritual propriety and held meetings at appointed times to promulgate prohibitions: these were indeed means of restraining unrighteousness. When prohibitions were not issued from above, but private meetings were held below, the established rules had already been violated. How much worse, then, to meet repeatedly and finally become estranged! In its dealings with Song, Lu did not stop at one meeting but proceeded to a second; it did not stop at two but went on to four. Their feelings toward one another could be called close. Why, then, did Lu immediately undertake war against Song? Before the covenant altars and ceremonial stands had been cleared away, they were already taking up arms; the bows and courtesies had scarcely begun before they became enemies. I fear that ritual propriety cannot be relied upon. What, then, can be relied upon to secure respect? The Sage…

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
懼夫世道之愈趨愈下也故于魯宋之盟會備
存而不削者若曰大道爲公講信脩睦爲事何
至于盟會之煩如此耶吁于以見聖人憂世之
心焉于以見聖人公天下之志焉又以見先王
望天下之厚焉何也先王非不知盟會非古道
也謂人心雖不古而天理之在人心者未泯故
不得巳設盟會之典使天下因盟以思信因會
以思敬庶亦不失乎大道之公也夫子之心其
先王之心乎不然何葵丘之盟束牲載書而不
歃血獨深取于齊桓耶
===
六月公會宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯
晉趙盾癸酉同盟于新城　文公十有四年
李光鸞
同考試官教諭蔡　批　〔尊王之義場中作者類多冗瑣〕
〔厭覩是作詞不繁而意自足可以占所養矣〕
考試官教諭盧　批　〔結說趙盾功罪明白〕
考試官學正丘　批　〔謹嚴〕
punctuated:
懼夫世道之愈趨愈下也，故于魯宋之盟會備存而不削者，若曰：「大道爲公，講信脩睦爲事，何至于盟會之煩如此耶？」吁！于以見聖人憂世之心焉，于以見聖人公天下之志焉，又以見先王望天下之厚焉。何也？先王非不知盟會非古道也，謂人心雖不古，而天理之在人心者未泯，故不得巳設盟會之典，使天下因盟以思信，因會以思敬，庶亦不失乎大道之公也。夫子之心，其先王之心乎？不然，何葵丘之盟束牲載書而不歃血，獨深取于齊桓耶？

六月，公會宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、晉趙盾，癸酉，同盟于新城。文公十有四年。

李光鸞

同考試官教諭蔡，批：〔尊王之義，場中作者類多冗瑣〕〔厭覩。是作詞不繁而意自足，可以占所養矣。〕

考試官教諭盧，批：〔結說趙盾功罪明白。〕

考試官學正丘，批：〔謹嚴。〕
translation_en:
…feared that the ways of the world were declining ever further. Thus he preserved a full record of the covenants and meetings between Lu and Song without deleting them, as if to say: “If the Great Way serves the common good, and people devote themselves to fostering trust and cultivating concord, how could covenants and meetings become so tiresomely numerous?” Ah! Here we see the sage’s concern for the world; here we see his resolve to make all under Heaven serve the common good; and here, too, we see the high expectations the former kings held for the world. Why is this? The former kings were not unaware that covenants and meetings were no part of the ancient Way. They believed that, although people’s hearts were no longer as they had been in antiquity, the heavenly principle within them had not disappeared. Thus, having no alternative, they established the institutions of covenants and meetings, so that covenants might prompt everyone under Heaven to reflect on trustworthiness, and meetings might prompt them to reflect on respect. In this way, they hoped that the impartiality of the Great Way might still be preserved. Was not the Master’s heart that of the former kings? Otherwise, why did he so particularly commend Duke Huan of Qi for the covenant at Kuiqiu, where the sacrificial animal was bound and the covenant document prepared, but no blood was smeared on the lips?

“In the sixth month, the duke met with the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, and Zhao Dun of Jin. On the guiyou day, they jointly covenanted at Xincheng.” Fourteenth year of Duke Wen.

Li Guangluan.

Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: “On the principle of honoring the king, the essays written in the examination hall are mostly so prolix and petty as to weary the reader. This essay uses few words yet fully conveys its meaning; from it one can judge the author’s cultivation.”

Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: “The concluding discussion clearly distinguishes Zhao Dun’s merits and faults.”

Examiner Qiu, School Instructor, comments: “Careful and rigorous.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
春秋予列國之從霸臣所以重尊王之義也蓋
晉雖不兢猶以尊周爲心何靳于諸侯之從之
此新城之盟所以書同以予之也何予夫新城
之盟之同也同外楚也蓋周室衰微天下安危
係于霸王室安危係于霸而梗王之化與中國
爲讎者莫楚若也文襄以來晉主夏盟城濮戰
而内外之防嚴踐土盟而尊王之義著周室固
恃以無恐矣維時楚莊强盛日懷窺伺浸浸乎
有北圖之勢何幸有新城之盟耶事出于懼心
===
之生信講夫禦楚之謀蓋有不約而同者雖曰
晉靈幼弱霸業弗振斯盟也若無敵于楚也然
即此可以見人心之有周焉中國之有人焉雖
曰趙盾主盟諸侯聽命是舉也若不可爲訓也
然即此可以見無主霸之君焉有輔霸之臣焉
春秋重周屬于重晉惡楚深于惡盾故于新城
之盟而特書同者若曰天下多趨于勢而昧夫
義晉楚强弱之勢雖殊諸侯向背之義甚明使
楚人知之而窺鼎之心或可少息矣是故予諸
punctuated: 春秋予列國之從霸臣，所以重尊王之義也。蓋晉雖不兢，猶以尊周爲心，何靳于諸侯之從之？此新城之盟所以書同以予之也。何予夫新城之盟之同也？同外楚也。蓋周室衰微，天下安危係于霸，王室安危係于霸，而梗王之化、與中國爲讎者，莫楚若也。文襄以來，晉主夏盟，城濮戰而内外之防嚴，踐土盟而尊王之義著，周室固恃以無恐矣。維時楚莊强盛，日懷窺伺，浸浸乎有北圖之勢，何幸有新城之盟耶！事出于懼心之生，信講夫禦楚之謀，蓋有不約而同者。雖曰晉靈幼弱，霸業弗振，斯盟也若無敵于楚也，然即此可以見人心之有周焉，中國之有人焉。雖曰趙盾主盟，諸侯聽命，是舉也若不可爲訓也，然即此可以見無主霸之君焉，有輔霸之臣焉。春秋重周屬于重晉，惡楚深于惡盾，故于新城之盟而特書同者，若曰：天下多趨于勢而昧夫義，晉楚强弱之勢雖殊，諸侯向背之義甚明，使楚人知之，而窺鼎之心或可少息矣。是故予諸
translation_en:
The Spring and Autumn Annals approves the various states’ following a hegemon’s minister because it gives weight to the duty of honoring the king. Although Jin was not strong enough to contend [?], it still cherished the intention of honoring Zhou. Why, then, withhold approval from the lords for following it? This is why the covenant at Xincheng is recorded as a “joint” covenant, thereby expressing approval. Why approve their acting jointly in the covenant at Xincheng? Because they joined in excluding Chu.

As the royal house of Zhou declined, the security of all under Heaven depended on the hegemon, and the security of the royal house likewise depended on the hegemon. Yet none rivaled Chu in obstructing the king’s civilizing influence and making enemies of the central states. Since the days of Dukes Wen and Xiang, Jin had presided over the covenants of the Xia states. The battle at Chengpu firmly established the boundary between those within and those without; the covenant at Jiantu made manifest the duty of honoring the king. The royal house of Zhou could indeed rely on these achievements and remain free from fear. At this time, King Zhuang of Chu was powerful and flourishing, constantly watching for an opportunity, and increasingly displaying ambitions toward the north. How fortunate that there was the covenant at Xincheng! It arose from a shared sense of fear. They earnestly discussed plans to resist Chu, reaching agreement without prior arrangement.

Granted, Duke Ling of Jin was young and weak, and Jin’s hegemony had failed to flourish; this alliance seemingly could not match Chu [?]. Nevertheless, it shows that people still held Zhou in their hearts and that the central states still had men capable of serving them. Granted, Zhao Dun presided over the covenant and the lords obeyed his commands, so that this undertaking seemingly could not serve as a proper precedent. Nevertheless, it shows that, though there was no ruler able to direct the hegemony, there was a minister able to sustain it.

The Spring and Autumn Annals’ regard for Zhou entails regard for Jin, and its condemnation of Chu runs deeper than its condemnation of Zhao Dun. Thus its special use of the word “joint” in recording the covenant at Xincheng is as though it were saying: Most people under Heaven gravitate toward power and fail to understand righteousness. Although Jin and Chu differed in strength, the lords’ duty concerning whom to support and whom to oppose was perfectly clear. If the men of Chu understood this, their desire to covet the royal tripods might abate somewhat. Thus, in granting approval to the various…

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
侯者非予其盟㸔也予其外楚以從晉也非予
其從晉也予其從晉以尊周也否則列國之盟
亦屢矣何獨于新城而予之抑是盟也固可爲
世道喜亦可爲紀綱惜周室恃以無恐中國恃
以少安謂非㸔之功不可也内專國政而外主
會盟㸔之權日重而晉靈之勢孤矣桃園之禍
寧不兆于此乎吁君子于㸔乎何誅
禮記
禮樂之說管乎人情矣
===
姜蓋
同考試官教諭王　批〔中正和平得禮樂之說者錄之〕
考試官教諭盧　批〔發揮管人情處明盡〕
考試官學正丘　批〔平順〕
〔以範多士〕
記者論禮樂之用而切于人焉夫易流易離者
人情也統同辨異而流離之失免矣禮樂非人
情之至切者哉樂記君子示天下之坊也蓋謂
不一者禮樂之體合一者禮樂之功是故本于
punctuated:
侯者，非予其盟㸔也，予其外楚以從晉也；非予其從晉也，予其從晉以尊周也。否則，列國之盟亦屢矣，何獨于新城而予之？抑是盟也，固可爲世道喜，亦可爲紀綱惜。周室恃以無恐，中國恃以少安，謂非㸔之功不可也。内專國政而外主會盟，㸔之權日重，而晉靈之勢孤矣。桃園之禍，寧不兆于此乎？吁！君子于㸔乎何誅？

禮記
禮樂之說，管乎人情矣。

姜蓋
同考試官教諭王　批〔中正和平，得禮樂之說者，錄之。〕
考試官教諭盧　批〔發揮管人情處明盡。〕
考試官學正丘　批〔平順。〕
〔以範多士〕

記者論禮樂之用，而切于人焉。夫易流易離者，人情也。統同辨異，而流離之失免矣。禮樂非人情之至切者哉？樂記：「君子示天下之坊也。」蓋謂不一者禮樂之體，合一者禮樂之功。是故本于
translation_en:
…the feudal lords are commended, not for their covenant with Zhao Dun [?; transcribed as 㸔], but for excluding Chu and following Jin; nor are they commended simply for following Jin, but for following Jin in order to honor Zhou. Otherwise, covenants among the various states were frequent: why commend this one at Xincheng alone? Yet this covenant, though certainly cause for rejoicing over the condition of the world, also gives cause to lament the state of governing order. The royal house of Zhou relied on it to be free from fear, and the central states relied on it for some measure of peace. One cannot deny that this was Dun’s achievement. Internally he monopolized the government of his state, while externally he presided over meetings and covenants. Dun’s power grew daily, while Duke Ling of Jin became isolated. Was not the calamity at the Peach Garden already foreshadowed here? Alas! For what should the gentleman condemn Dun?

Record of Rites
“The teachings of ritual and music govern human feelings.”

Jiang Gai
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “Balanced, correct, harmonious, and even-tempered; this essay grasps the teachings of ritual and music. Select it.”
Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: “Clearly and fully expounds the point about governing human feelings.”
Examiner Qiu, School Director, comments: “Even and fluent.”
[To provide a model for the many scholars.]

The author of the Record discusses the functions of ritual and music as matters intimately concerning human beings. Human feelings readily run to excess or drift apart. By bringing together what is shared and distinguishing what differs, these failings of excess and estrangement are avoided. Are ritual and music not, then, of the utmost relevance to human feelings? The Record of Music says: “The gentleman shows the world its safeguards.” [?] This means that ritual and music differ in their forms but are united in their effects. Thus, taking as their basis…

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
事理之著而爲品節之詳禮固不可易矣然使
人制節謹度秩然而不亂者皆禮之序爲之也
禮之說辨異盡之矣由于人心之動而爲中和
之感樂固不可變矣然使人和順道德純然而
罔間者皆樂之和統之也樂之說統同盡之矣
夫若此者何以爲人情之管耶蓋人情相親而
易至于流也惟禮以辨異則有義以相維而情
不敢以自肆親疎有序也貴賤有等也撙節退
讓之心而得於制度文爲之表矣是不一者人
===
之情隨時而有異也至一者禮之制防範而不
過也禮固緣情而制情寔由禮而中矣禮之道
非檢束人情之大節矣乎人情相敬而易至于
離也惟樂以統同則有恩以相與而情不容以
或乖佚能思初也安能惟始也忻喜歡愛之情
而得夫優柔中平之正矣是無常者人之情感
物而多變也有常者樂之理統紀而不亂也樂
固以情而作情寔因樂而治矣樂之道非管攝
人情之大端矣乎是則禮能飾貌而不流則合
punctuated:
事理之著而爲品節之詳，禮固不可易矣。然使人制節謹度，秩然而不亂者，皆禮之序爲之也。禮之說，辨異盡之矣。由于人心之動而爲中和之感，樂固不可變矣。然使人和順道德，純然而罔間者，皆樂之和統之也。樂之說，統同盡之矣。
夫若此者，何以爲人情之管耶？蓋人情相親而易至于流也，惟禮以辨異，則有義以相維，而情不敢以自肆。親疎有序也，貴賤有等也，撙節退讓之心，而得於制度文爲之表矣。是不一者，人之情隨時而有異也；至一者，禮之制防範而不過也。禮固緣情而制，情寔由禮而中矣。禮之道，非檢束人情之大節矣乎？人情相敬而易至于離也，惟樂以統同，則有恩以相與，而情不容以或乖。佚能思初也，安能惟始也，忻喜歡愛之情，而得夫優柔中平之正矣。是無常者，人之情感物而多變也；有常者，樂之理統紀而不亂也。樂固以情而作，情寔因樂而治矣。樂之道，非管攝人情之大端矣乎？是則禮能飾貌而不流，則合
translation_en:
…the manifest principles of affairs, elaborating them into detailed distinctions and regulations: ritual surely cannot be altered. Yet what enables people to regulate their conduct and observe proper measures, maintaining order without confusion, is entirely the ordering power of ritual. The meaning of ritual is fully expressed in “distinguishing differences.” Arising from the stirrings of the human heart and producing feelings of equilibrium and harmony, music surely cannot be changed. Yet what enables people to accord harmoniously with the Way and virtue, in undivided purity, is entirely the unifying power of music’s harmony. The meaning of music is fully expressed in “uniting in sameness.”
How, then, do these govern human feelings? Human feelings incline people toward mutual affection, but readily lead to excess. Only when ritual distinguishes differences does righteousness bind people together, so that their feelings dare not run unchecked. There is an order governing the close and the distant, and there are ranks distinguishing the noble and the lowly. A disposition toward restraint and deference thus finds outward expression in institutions, measures, and ceremonial conduct. What varies is human feeling, which differs with the circumstances; what remains wholly consistent is the regulation of ritual, which guards against transgression. Ritual is indeed fashioned in accordance with feelings, and feelings truly attain their proper balance through ritual. Is not the Way of ritual a great guiding principle for restraining human feelings? Human feelings incline people toward mutual respect, but readily lead to estrangement. Only when music unites people in sameness does kindness draw them together, so that their feelings cannot become discordant. In ease they can recall their beginnings; in security they can reflect upon their origins. Feelings of joy, delight, affection, and love thus attain the proper condition of gentleness, equilibrium, and evenness. What is inconstant is human feeling, which changes frequently in response to things; what is constant is the principle of music, which unifies and orders without confusion. Music is indeed created from feelings, and feelings truly become well ordered through music. Is not the Way of music a great means of governing human feelings? Thus ritual can refine outward demeanor and prevent excess; then, united [?]…

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
皆不爭矣樂能合情而不離則人皆無怨矣孰
謂禮樂而可斯須去身也哉抑禮樂之道雖切
於人情而禮樂之本則在於吾心吾之心正則
天地之心亦正吾之氣順則天地之氣亦順天
地位而禮樂與矣是故無體之禮禮之至也無
聲之樂樂之至也後世知不出此而徒從事於
儀文度數之末失之矣此綿蕞野外之習徒襲
秦之陋而桑間濮上之音實足爲導欲增悲之
助耳於人情何有哉然則欲明禮樂之教者必
===
建中和之極而後可
夫孝置之而塞乎天地溥之而横乎四海
施諸後世而無朝夕推而放諸東海而
準推而放諸西海而準推而放諸南海
而準推而放諸北海而準詩云自西自
東自南自北無思不服此之謂也
李羔
同考試官教諭王　批　孝爲人心同然故推無不準此
作辭約而意盡
punctuated:
皆不爭矣。樂能合情而不離，則人皆無怨矣。孰謂禮樂而可斯須去身也哉？抑禮樂之道雖切於人情，而禮樂之本則在於吾心。吾之心正，則天地之心亦正；吾之氣順，則天地之氣亦順。天地位，而禮樂與矣。是故無體之禮，禮之至也；無聲之樂，樂之至也。後世知不出此，而徒從事於儀文度數之末，失之矣。此綿蕞野外之習，徒襲秦之陋；而桑間濮上之音，實足爲導欲增悲之助耳，於人情何有哉？然則欲明禮樂之教者，必建中和之極而後可。
夫孝，置之而塞乎天地，溥之而横乎四海，施諸後世而無朝夕。推而放諸東海而準，推而放諸西海而準，推而放諸南海而準，推而放諸北海而準。《詩》云：「自西自東，自南自北，無思不服。」此之謂也。
李羔
同考試官教諭王　批：孝爲人心同然，故推無不準。此作辭約而意盡。
translation_en:
…all refrain from contention. When music harmonizes feelings without allowing estrangement, everyone is free of resentment. Who could say that rites and music may be dispensed with even for a moment? Yet although the way of rites and music closely concerns human feelings, their foundation lies in our own hearts. When my heart is correct, the heart of Heaven and Earth is also correct; when my vital energy is harmonious, the vital energy of Heaven and Earth is also harmonious. Heaven and Earth take their proper places, and rites and music participate therein. Thus rites without outward form are the highest rites, and music without sound is the highest music. In later ages, understanding did not go beyond this [?], and people merely occupied themselves with the secondary details of ceremonial forms and numerical regulations, thereby missing the essentials. Such rehearsals in the open countryside, using cords and reed markers, merely perpetuated the crude practices of Qin. The music of Sangjian and Pushang served only to incite desire and deepen sorrow. What benefit did these bring to human feelings? Thus those who wish to make clear the teaching of rites and music must first establish the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony.
As for filial piety: set it in place, and it fills Heaven and Earth; spread it abroad, and it extends across the Four Seas; apply it to later generations, and it holds at all times, morning and evening. Extend it to the Eastern Sea, and it accords with the standard; extend it to the Western Sea, and it accords with the standard; extend it to the Southern Sea, and it accords with the standard; extend it to the Northern Sea, and it accords with the standard. The Book of Odes says: “From the west and from the east, from the south and from the north, none failed to submit.” This is what it means.
Li Gao 李羔
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: Filial piety is something that all human hearts alike acknowledge; hence, wherever it is extended, it accords with the standard. This composition is concise in expression yet exhaustive in meaning.

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭盧　批〔得曾子論孝之旨〕
考試官學正丘　批〔通暢〕
大賢言孝道之大達無不順而明以詩焉夫其
大無外者孝也然推之無不準者豈非以人心
之所同哉昔曾子之意蓋謂立人之道有孝焉
天性無俟于外求至理不假於強合其至大者
乎彼莫大于天地也惟孝無限量極乎天而蟠
乎地上下同流充周而不可窮矣莫廣于四海
也惟孝無方體足于此而充于彼溥博無涯廣
===
大而不可禦矣莫遠于後世也惟孝無終窮立
于百世之上驗于百世之下悠久無疆貫今古
於不息也何朝夕之間乎夫孝在天下雖至大
而無外然理在人心則至順而無逆故推而放
諸東海也西海也同此心則同此孝效法以事
親者不過率其性分之良耳不必應僾志之化固
不因地而有殊矣推而放諸南海也北海也此
□同則此孝同觀感以盡孝者不過充其固有
□善耳秉彝懿德之好罔不異地而同乎矣詩
punctuated:
考試官教諭盧，批〔得曾子論孝之旨〕。
考試官學正丘，批〔通暢〕。
大賢言孝道之大，達無不順，而明以詩焉。夫其大無外者，孝也。然推之無不準者，豈非以人心之所同哉？昔曾子之意，蓋謂立人之道有孝焉，天性無俟于外求，至理不假於強合，其至大者乎！彼莫大于天地也，惟孝無限量，極乎天而蟠乎地，上下同流，充周而不可窮矣。莫廣于四海也，惟孝無方體，足于此而充于彼，溥博無涯，廣大而不可禦矣。莫遠于後世也，惟孝無終窮，立于百世之上，驗于百世之下，悠久無疆，貫今古於不息也，何朝夕之間乎？夫孝在天下，雖至大而無外，然理在人心，則至順而無逆。故推而放諸東海也、西海也，同此心則同此孝，效法以事親者，不過率其性分之良耳。不必應僾志之化，固不因地而有殊矣。推而放諸南海也、北海也，此□同則此孝同，觀感以盡孝者，不過充其固有□善耳。秉彝懿德之好，罔不異地而同乎矣。詩
translation_en:
Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: 〔Captures the purport of Zengzi’s discussion of filial piety.〕
Examiner Qiu, Instructor, comments: 〔Clear and fluent.〕
The great worthy speaks of the greatness of the Way of filial piety: wherever it reaches, all accord with it. He elucidates this with the Book of Odes. What is so great that nothing lies outside it is filial piety. Yet when extended, it serves as a standard everywhere—is this not because it rests on what human hearts share? Zengzi’s meaning was surely that filial piety belongs to the Way by which one establishes oneself as a human being. Inherent in our nature, it need not be sought outside ourselves; as the ultimate principle, it requires no forced conformity. Is it not supremely great?
Nothing is greater than Heaven and Earth. Yet filial piety knows no limit: it reaches to Heaven and extends throughout Earth, flowing alike above and below, pervading everything inexhaustibly. Nothing is broader than the Four Seas. Yet filial piety has no fixed location or form: sufficient here, it fills that place too, spreading boundlessly, so vast that nothing can restrain it. Nothing is more distant than later generations. Yet filial piety has no end: established a hundred generations ago, it is verified a hundred generations hence. Enduring without limit, it runs unceasingly through past and present. How could it be confined to the span of a morning or an evening?
Although filial piety in the world is supremely great, with nothing outside it, its principle resides in human hearts, where it is wholly harmonious and encounters no resistance. Thus, when extended to the eastern and western seas, wherever there is this same heart, there is this same filial piety. Those who follow its example in serving their parents merely follow the goodness inherent in their nature. They need not respond to a transforming influence upon their cherished intentions [?]; filial piety certainly does not differ according to place. When extended to the southern and northern seas, where this [illegible character] is the same, this filial piety is also the same. Those who fulfill their filial duties through observing others and being moved by their example merely develop their inherent goodness [one character illegible]. The love of constant moral principles and admirable virtue is shared everywhere, despite differences of place. The Book of Odes…

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
不云乎自西自東自南自北無思不服蓋言民
心之服王化文德所被一出于心悅之誠其郎
人心之從孝道風聲所曁同率乎順德之應者
之謂歟夫原其始本乎事親之常要其終極乎
感化之大如此君子可不充吾孝之大而立人
紀之極哉抑底豫之道盡而大定之化成四方
攸同乃遹追來孝者以先之也然舜文豈爲天
下以孝其親而天下亦豈以孝悅舜文哉雖聖
人固不能強天下以所性之無而天下亦不能
===
加毫末于性分之外道本至足各足焉爾矣聖
人不過先得民心同然者以導之耳況良心眞
切莫先于孝而天經地義莫大于孝導之豈有
不從者哉故曰聖王以孝治天下
第貳場
論
君子深造之以道
謝滄
同考試官教諭廖　批〔孟子示人造道之方自得處極〕
punctuated:
不云乎：「自西自東，自南自北，無思不服。」蓋言民心之服王化，文德所被，一出于心悅之誠。其郎人心之從孝道，風聲所曁，同率乎順德之應者之謂歟？夫原其始，本乎事親之常；要其終，極乎感化之大。如此，君子可不充吾孝之大，而立人紀之極哉？抑底豫之道盡，而大定之化成，四方攸同，乃遹追來孝者以先之也。然舜文豈爲天下以孝其親，而天下亦豈以孝悅舜文哉？雖聖人，固不能強天下以所性之無，而天下亦不能加毫末于性分之外。道本至足，各足焉爾矣。聖人不過先得民心同然者以導之耳。況良心眞切，莫先于孝；而天經地義，莫大于孝。導之，豈有不從者哉？故曰：「聖王以孝治天下。」

第貳場
論
君子深造之以道
謝滄

同考試官教諭廖，批〔孟子示人造道之方，自得處極〕
translation_en:
…does it not say: “From the west, from the east, from the south, from the north, none thought of withholding submission”? This speaks of the people’s hearts submitting to kingly transformation: wherever civil virtue reaches, their submission springs entirely from sincere delight in their hearts. Does this mean [?] that, wherever the influence of filial conduct reaches, people’s hearts follow the way of filial piety, all responding alike to virtue in accordance with their nature? Trace it to its beginning, and it is rooted in the ordinary practice of serving one’s parents; consider its ultimate outcome, and it culminates in the greatness of moral transformation. This being so, can the gentleman fail to develop the full greatness of his filial piety and establish the highest standard of human relationships? When the way of bringing one’s parents to contentment is fully realized, the transforming influence that brings great stability is accomplished, and all regions are united. It is those who follow their forebears and carry forward filial devotion who lead the way. Yet did Shun and King Wen practice filial piety toward their parents for the sake of the realm? And did the people of the realm practice filial piety to please Shun and King Wen? Even sages cannot compel everyone to possess what is absent from their nature [?], nor can anyone add the slightest thing beyond what their nature allots them. The Way is inherently wholly sufficient; each person possesses that sufficiency, and that is all. Sages merely grasp first what all people’s hearts affirm in common and use it to guide them. Moreover, among the genuine impulses of the moral heart, none takes precedence over filial piety; among the constant principles of Heaven and the proper obligations of Earth, none is greater than filial piety. When people are guided by it, how could any fail to follow? Thus it is said: “The sage kings govern the realm through filial piety.”

Second Session

“The gentleman pursues profound attainment by following the Way.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
難摸寫此篇發揮明盡且純正爾雅亦深造自得者敬服
考試官教諭盧　批　脫去奇僻語自是大家數文字
考試官學正丘　批　典重不浮
論曰君子入聖之學無他亦惟有不容已之功
不可紊之序而已何謂功有定向也何謂序有
定守也相須並用不可缺一者也功深而乖其
序則誕誕則滯序章而闕其功則踈踈則廢君
子之學荒矣求以入聖也不亦難乎立志以定
其趨而弗躐於進取循序以要其成而弗惰於
===
中道優游涵泳默識心通由是而居之安由是
而資之深由是而取之左右逢其原推人以之
天優入於聖域斯理之所必至者也茲其爲君
子之學也請竟其說理之在天下廣大悉備其
用也靜深玄妙其體也可以力造不可以淺求
可以漸進不可以驟入可以神悟不可以強得
自夫天下之大聖聰明睿知而神化通成性存
存而道義出靜與天俱動與天游固不假於學
習矣人不皆聖人也下學之功可容已乎君子
punctuated:
難摸寫，此篇發揮明盡，且純正爾雅，亦深造自得者，敬服。
考試官教諭盧批：脫去奇僻語，自是大家數文字。
考試官學正丘批：典重不浮。
論曰：君子入聖之學，無他，亦惟有不容已之功、不可紊之序而已。何謂功？有定向也。何謂序？有定守也。相須並用，不可缺一者也。功深而乖其序，則誕，誕則滯；序章而闕其功，則踈，踈則廢。君子之學荒矣，求以入聖也，不亦難乎？立志以定其趨，而弗躐於進取；循序以要其成，而弗惰於中道。優游涵泳，默識心通，由是而居之安，由是而資之深，由是而取之左右逢其原。推人以之天，優入於聖域，斯理之所必至者也。茲其爲君子之學也，請竟其說。理之在天下，廣大悉備，其用也；靜深玄妙，其體也。可以力造，不可以淺求；可以漸進，不可以驟入；可以神悟，不可以強得。自夫天下之大聖，聰明睿知而神化通，成性存存而道義出，靜與天俱，動與天游，固不假於學習矣。人不皆聖人也，下學之功可容已乎？君子
translation_en:
…is difficult to portray. This essay expounds it clearly and exhaustively; moreover, its language is pure, correct, and refined. Its author, too, has pursued learning deeply and attained understanding for himself. I admire him respectfully.
Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: “Free of strange and eccentric expressions, this is assuredly writing of a master's caliber.”
Examiner Qiu, School Director, comments: “Classical and dignified, without superficiality.”
The discourse states: The learning through which the gentleman enters sagehood consists of nothing other than effort that must never cease and a sequence that must never be disordered. What is meant by effort? Having a settled direction. What is meant by sequence? Having a fixed course to maintain. These depend upon each other and must be employed together; neither can be dispensed with. If effort is profound but departs from its proper sequence, it becomes extravagant, and extravagance leads to stagnation. If the sequence is clear but effort is lacking, learning becomes lax, and laxity leads to abandonment. The gentleman's learning then falls into neglect. Would it not be difficult to seek entry into sagehood in this way? He establishes his resolve to fix his course, without skipping stages in his advance; he follows the proper sequence to secure completion, without growing idle midway. At ease, he immerses himself in learning, silently apprehending it and understanding it in his heart. Through this he dwells securely in it; through this he draws deeply upon it; through this, wherever he turns to draw upon it, he encounters its source. Extending the human to reach Heaven [?], he enters the realm of sagehood with ease: this is the outcome to which principle necessarily leads. Such is the gentleman's learning. Allow me to explain it fully.
Principle as it exists throughout the world is vast and all-encompassing in its functioning, still, profound, mysterious, and subtle in its substance. It can be reached through strenuous effort, but cannot be sought superficially; one can advance toward it gradually, but cannot enter it abruptly; it can be apprehended through spiritual insight, but cannot be obtained by force. As for the world's great sages, their acuity and sagacious understanding penetrate spiritual transformation; they continually preserve their fully realized nature, and the Way and righteousness issue forth. In stillness they abide with Heaven; in movement they roam with Heaven. They assuredly have no need to rely upon study and practice. Yet not everyone is a sage. Can the effort of learning elementary matters ever be allowed to cease? The gentleman…

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
學聖人者也使學聖人而不得其所以學則亦
徒焉而已求以至於聖人也得乎君子亦審之
素矣是故有深造之功焉有以道之序焉有自
得之妙焉爲入聖之學焉自夫人之不知君子
之學也用力於皮膚之粗責效於旦暮之間從
事於虛無之中安意於言意之表或欲速以求
達或急遽而躐等夫造道之功弗深則悟道之
機弗露造道之序弗循則會道之神弗融吾見
齟齬扞格鑿鑿乎其不相入矣君子之學不若
===
是之疎且誕也以聖人爲標準以至善爲歸宿
以剛毅爲己任志奮於必爲功期於必就不安
於小成不狃於近利如射者之的也行者之家
也江漢之歸宗也一息尚存此志不容少懈也
又能步趨不失其則仰止必守其度功有所當
加智有所不用知可致也精義入神不可驟也
行可力也利用安身不可遽也大可爲也化不
可爲也優游以俟其入也漸漬以待其成也下
學之功盡而上達之自致也成章而後達也盈
punctuated: 學聖人者也。使學聖人而不得其所以學，則亦徒焉而已，求以至於聖人也，得乎？君子亦審之素矣。是故有深造之功焉，有以道之序焉，有自得之妙焉，爲入聖之學焉。自夫人之不知君子之學也，用力於皮膚之粗，責效於旦暮之間，從事於虛無之中，安意於言意之表，或欲速以求達，或急遽而躐等。夫造道之功弗深，則悟道之機弗露；造道之序弗循，則會道之神弗融。吾見齟齬扞格，鑿鑿乎其不相入矣。君子之學不若是之疎且誕也。以聖人爲標準，以至善爲歸宿，以剛毅爲己任，志奮於必爲，功期於必就。不安於小成，不狃於近利，如射者之的也，行者之家也，江漢之歸宗也。一息尚存，此志不容少懈也。又能步趨不失其則，仰止必守其度，功有所當加，智有所不用。知可致也，精義入神不可驟也；行可力也，利用安身不可遽也；大可爲也，化不可爲也。優游以俟其入也，漸漬以待其成也。下學之功盡，而上達之自致也。成章而後達也，盈
translation_en: …is one who studies to become a sage. If one studies to become a sage without grasping how to undertake that learning, one merely labors in vain. Could one thereby attain sagehood? The gentleman has long considered this carefully. Thus there is the sustained effort of profound study, the proper sequence of proceeding according to the Way, and the subtle achievement of grasping it for oneself: these constitute the learning by which one enters sagehood. Those who do not understand the gentleman’s learning expend their effort on superficial matters, demand results overnight, occupy themselves with emptiness and nothingness, and rest content with what lies beyond words and meaning. Some seek swift attainment through haste; others rush ahead and skip stages. If the effort to advance in the Way is not profound, the opening for awakening to it will not appear; if the sequence of advancing in the Way is not followed, the spirit through which one comprehends it will not achieve integration. I see only discord and obstruction, things standing rigidly apart and failing to fit together. The gentleman’s learning is not so careless and fanciful. He takes the sage as his standard, the highest good as his destination, and firmness and resolution as his own responsibility. He rouses his determination to act without fail and directs his efforts toward certain accomplishment. He does not rest content with minor achievements or become habituated to immediate gains. His goal is like the archer’s target, the traveler’s home, or the sea to which the Jiang and Han rivers return. So long as a single breath remains, this resolve must not slacken in the least. Moreover, in every step he keeps to the proper rules, and in looking upward to his ideal he invariably observes the proper measures. There are matters to which effort must be applied, and matters in which cleverness has no use. Knowledge can be extended, but refining one’s understanding of principles until one penetrates the spiritual cannot be accomplished suddenly. Conduct can be pursued with effort, but making one’s actions beneficial and establishing oneself securely cannot be hurried. Greatness can be achieved through striving, but transformation cannot be produced by striving. One proceeds at ease, awaiting entry, and becomes gradually steeped in learning, awaiting its fulfillment. When the work of learning what is below has been fully accomplished, comprehension of what is above comes of itself. Only after completing a coherent whole does one advance; only after filling…

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
科而後進也君子之學不亦善於入聖矣乎夫
惟其有入聖之學也自得之效斯有不期然而
然者矣道明於發憤强學之餘理融於眞積力
久之後處之安固而不搖也資之深遠而無盡
也取之左右逢其原無所往而不值其所資之
本也於父子值吾自得之仁也於君臣值吾自
得之義也於賓主值吾自得之禮也於賢否值
吾自得之智也天道高遠難測亦無不與之脗
合也自食息起居之微推極於事物無窮之變
===
家國天下之異地也親踈貴賤之殊等也常變
經權之異施也無所往而不值其所資之本也
一本而散於萬殊也萬殊而歸於一本也所謂
從心所欲不踰矩也所謂溥博淵泉而時出之
也所謂施於四體四體不言而喻也至是不知
其孰爲君子也孰爲聖人也合安勉於同歸貫
天人於一致也君子之學會其全矣玆其爲入
聖之學也抑求之孔門善入聖之學者顏曾之
外不多見也心齋坐忘未見其止眞積力久竟
punctuated: 科而後進也。君子之學，不亦善於入聖矣乎？夫惟其有入聖之學也，自得之效，斯有不期然而然者矣。道明於發憤强學之餘，理融於眞積力久之後。處之安固而不搖也，資之深遠而無盡也，取之左右逢其原，無所往而不值其所資之本也。於父子，值吾自得之仁也；於君臣，值吾自得之義也；於賓主，值吾自得之禮也；於賢否，值吾自得之智也。天道高遠難測，亦無不與之脗合也。自食息起居之微，推極於事物無窮之變，家國天下之異地也，親踈貴賤之殊等也，常變經權之異施也，無所往而不值其所資之本也。一本而散於萬殊也，萬殊而歸於一本也。所謂從心所欲不踰矩也，所謂溥博淵泉而時出之也，所謂施於四體，四體不言而喻也。至是不知其孰爲君子也，孰爲聖人也。合安勉於同歸，貫天人於一致也。君子之學，會其全矣。玆其爲入聖之學也。抑求之孔門，善入聖之學者，顏曾之外不多見也。心齋坐忘，未見其止；眞積力久，竟
translation_en: …the hollows before advancing. Is not the learning of the exemplary person well suited to entering sagehood? Precisely because his learning leads into sagehood, the effects of attaining understanding for himself arise without his expecting them. The Way becomes clear after resolute, strenuous study; principles become integrated after genuine accumulation and prolonged effort. He abides in this understanding securely and unshakably, and draws upon it deeply and inexhaustibly. Drawing from it on either side, he encounters its source: wherever he goes, he encounters the root upon which he relies. In relations between father and son, he encounters the benevolence he has attained for himself; between ruler and minister, the righteousness he has attained for himself; between guest and host, the ritual propriety he has attained for himself; in distinguishing the worthy from the unworthy, the wisdom he has attained for himself. Though the Way of Heaven is lofty, remote, and hard to fathom, his understanding accords with it in every respect. From the minutiae of eating, resting, rising, and retiring, he extends this understanding to the inexhaustible changes of affairs and things: the different spheres of family, state, and all under Heaven; the different degrees of closeness and distance, nobility and lowliness; and the different applications appropriate to ordinary and exceptional circumstances, constant principles and discretionary judgment. Wherever he goes, he encounters the root upon which he relies. The single root branches into myriad differences, and myriad differences return to the single root. This is what is meant by “following the heart’s desires without overstepping the bounds”; by “being broad and all-embracing, deep as a wellspring, and bringing it forth at the proper time”; and by “manifesting it in the four limbs, which convey it without words.” At this point one cannot tell which is the exemplary person and which the sage. Those who practice with ease and those who exert themselves reach the same destination; Heaven and humanity are united in a single coherence. The learning of the exemplary person has attained its completeness. Such is the learning that leads into sagehood. Yet if we seek among the disciples of Confucius those adept at learning that leads into sagehood, few are to be found beyond Yan Hui and Zeng Shen. In “fasting the mind” and “sitting in forgetfulness,” we do not see the ultimate resting place [?]; through genuine accumulation and prolonged effort, ultimately …

punctuated:
以曾得造斯深矣。慱約之訓，忠恕之旨，能以道矣。卒之見道體於卓爾，悟一貫於無疑，自得之妙，可容已耶？他如悅道而畫，不可以言深；見小欲速，不可以言道。仰視顔曾，瞠若乎其後矣。欲其自得以入聖也，不亦難哉？孔子曰：「譬如爲山，未成一簣，止，吾止也。」又曰：「中人以下，不可以語上也。」玆固深造以道之敎也。孟子之論，其亦善學孔子者乎？
表
擬宋賜輔臣御製《瑞聖園觀稼》《城南觀麥》詩謝表〔祥符九年〕
東㮚
同考試官敎諭魏批〔於觀遊賦咏中發重農意，謝不忘規，心乎忠愛者也。欽服。〕
考試官敎諭盧批〔佳麗而謹嚴，得體。〕
考試官學正丘批〔典潤鏗鏘。〕
祥符九年〔某〕月〔某〕日，〔某〕官〔臣〕〔某〕等，伏蒙聖恩，頒賜御製《瑞聖園觀稼》《城南觀麥》詩，〔臣〕等
translation_en:
…Zeng was thereby able to attain such depth [?]. Through the teaching of broad learning and restraint, and the purport of conscientiousness and reciprocity, they were able to proceed according to the Way. In the end, one perceived the substance of the Way standing loftily before him, and the other understood without doubt the single thread running through it all. Could the marvel of attaining understanding for oneself ever cease? Others, who delight in the Way but set limits to their progress, cannot be said to reach depth; those who attend to petty gains and desire quick results cannot be said to follow the Way. Looking up toward Yan and Zeng, they stare from far behind. Is it not difficult to expect them to attain understanding for themselves and thereby enter sagehood? Confucius said: “It is like building a mound: if I stop when it lacks a single basketful, it is I who stop.” He also said: “Those below average cannot be told of higher things.” These are indeed teachings on advancing deeply through the proper Way. Does not Mencius’s discussion likewise show that he learned well from Confucius?
Memorial
A model memorial of thanks on behalf of Song chief ministers upon receiving the imperially composed poems “Viewing the Crops in Ruisheng Garden” and “Viewing the Wheat South of the City” 〔Ninth year of Xiangfu〕
Dong Li 東㮚
Comment by Associate Examiner Wei, Instructor: 〔Amid sightseeing and poetic composition, he brings out the importance of agriculture. In giving thanks, he does not forget admonition: his heart is devoted to loyalty and loving concern for the ruler. Admirable.〕
Comment by Examiner Lu, Instructor: 〔Elegant and beautiful, yet careful and disciplined; appropriate to the form.〕
Comment by Examiner Qiu, School Instructor: 〔Classically refined, polished, and sonorous.〕

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
謹拜受者百穀順成
上帝溥明昭之賜
六飛豫動
聖人敷茂對之章
頒布臣工昭回籞禁臣等誠懽誠忭稽首頓
首上言伏以貽我來牟詩頌思文之德先
知稼穡書垂無逸之規無麥特筆于麟經
有秋載書于月令粤惟前哲均重民天多
黍多稌之篇風斯厚矣于耜于茅之詠善
===
可稽焉兲道既荒醇音不作間有摛詞而
振響或忘務本以力田汾水秋風蘭菊何
裨于粒食蒲津曉渡山河未切于厚生焉
知小人之依豈念先民之作茲蓋伏遇
○○○○
道由學植
德本天成心弘穀種之仁治取嘉禾之喻養
賢四簋耕籍三推澶淵兵振以康民梁父
祀成于禱歲蝗飛溟渤聽億兆之謳歌雨
punctuated: 謹拜受者。百穀順成，上帝溥明昭之賜；六飛豫動，聖人敷茂對之章。頒布臣工，昭回籞禁。臣等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首上言：伏以貽我來牟，詩頌思文之德；先知稼穡，書垂無逸之規。無麥特筆于麟經，有秋載書于月令。粤惟前哲，均重民天。多黍多稌之篇，風斯厚矣；于耜于茅之詠，善可稽焉。兲道既荒，醇音不作。間有摛詞而振響，或忘務本以力田。汾水秋風，蘭菊何裨于粒食？蒲津曉渡，山河未切于厚生。焉知小人之依？豈念先民之作？茲蓋伏遇○○○○，道由學植，德本天成。心弘穀種之仁，治取嘉禾之喻。養賢四簋，耕籍三推。澶淵兵振以康民，梁父祀成于禱歲。蝗飛溟渤，聽億兆之謳歌；雨
translation_en:
…we have reverently bowed and received them. The hundred grains ripen in due season: the Lord on High widely bestows his manifest favor. The imperial six-horse carriage sets forth in joyful progress: the sage sovereign unfolds verses that splendidly answer Heaven’s gifts. Distributed among his servants and officials, their radiance shines throughout the palace precincts. We, your servants, rejoice and exult; bowing low and knocking our heads upon the ground, we submit these words:

We humbly reflect that, with “He bequeathed to us wheat and barley,” the Book of Odes praises the virtue celebrated in “The Accomplished”; with “First understand sowing and reaping,” the Book of Documents transmits the admonition of “Against Luxurious Ease.” The failure of the wheat harvest receives special notice in the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Classic of the Unicorn; a plentiful harvest is recorded in the Monthly Ordinances. The wise men of old all valued food as the people’s Heaven. In the verses on abundant millet and rice, their influence was indeed generous; in the songs of ploughshares and thatching grass, their goodness can be examined. Once the Way of Heaven had fallen into neglect, such pure strains were heard no more. Occasionally someone composed ornate verses and made his voice resound, yet perhaps forgot to attend to the fundamental occupation and labor in the fields. In “Autumn Wind” on the Fen River, what benefit did orchids and chrysanthemums bring to feeding the people with grain? In “Crossing Pujin at Dawn,” mountains and rivers had little direct bearing on enriching the people’s livelihood. How could such writers understand what common people depend upon? Did they give thought to the labors of their forebears?

Now we have humbly encountered ○○○○ [the sovereign’s designation is untranscribed], whose Way is rooted in learning and whose virtue is naturally endowed by Heaven. Your heart extends the benevolence embodied in a seed of grain; your governance takes the auspicious grain as its guiding analogy. You nourish worthy men with four ritual vessels of food, and plough the imperial field with three pushes of the plough. At Chanyuan, military might was displayed to bring peace to the people; at Liangfu, the sacrifice was accomplished in prayer for a fruitful year. Locusts flew away over the vast sea, and the songs of praise of the countless multitudes were heard; rain…

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
降星壇信
穹蒼之感格惟登聞妙于一德故大有協乎三
農嘉生並衍于近郊協氣攸同于上苑芃芃
芃惟麥將銍艾之奄觀或或其禾知億秭
之盈止迺命倌人而夙駕爰諏穀旦以來
游
天仗遥瞻式副何休之望
龍輿至止庸舒省歛之懷
皇覽欣榮
===
帝心嘉豈肆永言而見志因卽事以陶情一豫
一遊上繼卷阿之盛迹以南以雅遥追良
耜之徽音寫風物以入瑤篇擷英華而歸
藻思霞光日麗宣五色以成文玉振金聲
諧八風而從律蓋天地淳和之化不言而
四時行乃
聖人精蘊之神有作而萬物覩將竹史傳之永
世忽珍賜出自
尚方宜九奏以入鈞韶先十行而頒
punctuated: 降星壇，信穹蒼之感格。惟登聞妙于一德，故大有協乎三農。嘉生並衍于近郊，協氣攸同于上苑。芃芃芃惟麥，將銍艾之奄觀；或或其禾，知億秭之盈止。迺命倌人而夙駕，爰諏穀旦以來游。天仗遥瞻，式副何休之望；龍輿至止，庸舒省歛之懷。皇覽欣榮，帝心嘉豈。肆永言而見志，因卽事以陶情。一豫一遊，上繼《卷阿》之盛迹；以南以雅，遥追《良耜》之徽音。寫風物以入瑤篇，擷英華而歸藻思。霞光日麗，宣五色以成文；玉振金聲，諧八風而從律。蓋天地淳和之化，不言而四時行；乃聖人精蘊之神，有作而萬物覩。將竹史傳之永世，忽珍賜出自尚方。宜九奏以入鈞韶，先十行而頒
translation_en:
…descends upon the star altar, truly showing that the appeal has moved Heaven. Because the wondrous efficacy of making oneself heard above rests upon undivided virtue, abundant harvests bring blessings to all agricultural work. Fine crops flourish together in the nearby countryside, and harmonious vital energies likewise pervade the imperial park. Luxuriant, luxuriant is the wheat: soon its reaping with sickles will be seen everywhere. The grain stands thick [?], promising stores filled with countless measures. You therefore commanded the carriage attendants to harness the horses early, and chose an auspicious morning for your visit. The imperial escort could be seen from afar, fulfilling the hopes expressed by He Xiu; the dragon carriage arrived, giving expression to your concern to inspect the harvest. Your imperial gaze delighted in the flourishing growth; your sovereign heart rejoiced.

Then you expressed your aspirations in verse, cultivating your feelings through the scene before you. Each excursion and outing carried forward the splendid precedent of “The Winding Mound” (Juan e); in the manner of the Southern Airs and the Elegantiae, your verse distantly followed the excellent strains of “The Good Ploughshare” (Liang si). You depicted the landscape in precious verses, gathering its finest beauties into richly adorned thoughts. Like rosy clouds and radiant sunshine, the five colors unfolded into patterned brilliance; like the ringing of jade chimes and bronze bells, the sounds harmonized with the winds of all eight directions and accorded with musical pitch. Through Heaven and Earth’s pure and harmonious transforming influence, the four seasons proceed without a word; through the spiritual power of the sage’s innermost understanding, a work is brought forth and all things become manifest.

As this was about to be recorded in the annals for transmission to all future ages, a precious gift suddenly issued from the Directorate for Imperial Accoutrements. Fittingly, the verses should enter the celestial Shao music in nine performances; first, however, they were promulgated in ten lines of…

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
御札丹書乍啓光分
黼座之前白雪高吟慶溢掖垣之直竊念臣等
職慚素食分擬明農擊壤興歌載詠農夫
之慶含嬉戴德仰歸
天子之功欽大雅而三復彌深思賡歌而一詞
莫措未伸芹獻愧同草木之無知願竭葵
誠誓荅乾坤之有造伏願
化弘允殖
道法資生虞帝五絃永念民財之可阜豳風
===
王業之攸基萬年綿瓜瓞之徵自今伊始九
有繫苞桑之固裕後無疆臣等無任瞻
七月重惟
天仰
聖欣戴屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁場
punctuated:
御札。丹書乍啓，光分黼座之前；白雪高吟，慶溢掖垣之直。竊念臣等職慚素食，分擬明農。擊壤興歌，載詠農夫之慶；含嬉戴德，仰歸天子之功。欽大雅而三復彌深，思賡歌而一詞莫措。未伸芹獻，愧同草木之無知；願竭葵誠，誓荅乾坤之有造。伏願化弘允殖，道法資生。虞帝五絃，永念民財之可阜；豳風王業之攸基。萬年綿瓜瓞之徵，自今伊始；九有繫苞桑之固，裕後無疆。臣等無任瞻七月重惟天仰聖欣戴屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叁場
translation_en:
…the imperial autograph. As the vermilion writing is first unfolded, radiance spreads before the embroidered throne; as the lofty strains of “White Snow” are sung, rejoicing overflows the palace offices where we serve.
We humbly reflect that we, your servants, are ashamed to draw our stipends without rendering worthy service; our proper lot would be to devote ourselves to farming. Striking the earth and raising a song, we celebrate anew the farmers’ joy; rejoicing and cherishing your beneficence, we ascribe these achievements to the Son of Heaven. Reverently reading your lofty verse three times, our admiration deepens; wishing to continue your song, we cannot frame a single phrase. Having yet to present our humble offering of cress, we are ashamed to be as uncomprehending as grass and trees. We wish to exhaust our sunflower-like devotion, pledging to repay the creative beneficence of Heaven and Earth.
We humbly wish that your transforming influence may spread widely and foster abundant growth, and that your Way may take as its model the power that nurtures life. Like the emperor of Yu with his five-stringed zither, may you ever remember that the people’s wealth can be increased; in the Airs of Bin lies the foundation of kingly achievement. May the auspicious promise of melons great and small—an enduring succession of descendants—extend for ten thousand years, beginning now; may the Nine Domains be secured as firmly as though bound to the roots of a mulberry, enriching posterity without limit. We, your servants, look toward Heaven and gaze up to Your Sagely Majesty with boundless joy, devotion, and trembling reverence [?: the transmitted text here contains the displaced or garbled words “Seventh Month, ponder anew”]. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our thanks and make them known to Your Majesty.
Third Session

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
策
第一問
馮顯
同考試官教諭熊　批　〔敷政以仁典學以心此〕
聖人文之有本者子能鋪張揚厲而詞藻蔚然
同考試官教授馬　批　〔體裁峻整敷揚明備忠愛之心〕
聖化作人之深可仰見矣
考試官教諭盧　批　〔揄揚其悉是涵濡〕
〔愽洽之學具見之矣錄之不獨以其文也〕
===
考試官學正丘　批　〔敷對詳明〕
聖化而有得者
聖人之御天下也有經世之文有範世之
文經世之文詔令是也而莫非仁政之敷
範世之文製作是也而莫非心學之著何
者治本于道而仁固道之實也學以基治
而心則學之源也脩道以仁則如天之化
成而大業裕典學以心則如天之於穆而
大道神是故積厚而章本植而茂英華發
punctuated:
策
第一問
馮顯

同考試官教諭熊　批　〔敷政以仁，典學以心，此〕聖人文之有本者。子能鋪張揚厲，而詞藻蔚然。

同考試官教授馬　批　〔體裁峻整，敷揚明備，忠愛之心〕聖化作人之深，可仰見矣。

考試官教諭盧　批　〔揄揚其悉，是涵濡〕〔愽洽之學，具見之矣。錄之不獨以其文也。〕

考試官學正丘　批　〔敷對詳明〕聖化而有得者。

聖人之御天下也，有經世之文，有範世之文。經世之文，詔令是也，而莫非仁政之敷；範世之文，製作是也，而莫非心學之著。何者？治本于道，而仁固道之實也；學以基治，而心則學之源也。脩道以仁，則如天之化成，而大業裕；典學以心，則如天之於穆，而大道神。是故積厚而章，本植而茂，英華發…
translation_en:
Policy Essay
First Question
Feng Xian

Comment by Associate Examiner Xiong, Instructor: “To extend government through benevolence and direct learning through the mind: these give the sage’s writings their foundation. You have elaborated and extolled this splendidly, with a rich flowering of literary expression.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Ma, Professor: “The composition is rigorous and well ordered; its exposition is clear and comprehensive. A heart of loyalty and love [connection uncertain, ?]. Here one may reverently perceive how profoundly the sage’s transforming influence nurtures men of talent.”

Comment by Examiner Lu, Instructor: “Its praise is exhaustive; this is the result of immersion [?]. Broad and comprehensive learning is fully apparent here. We select it not solely for its literary accomplishment.”

Comment by Examiner Qiu, Instructor: “The response is detailed and lucid—one who has gained from the sage’s transforming influence [?].”

In governing all under Heaven, the sage has writings that order the world and writings that serve as models for the world. The writings that order the world are edicts and commands, all of which extend benevolent government. The writings that serve as models for the world are his compositions, all of which manifest the learning of the mind. Why is this? Government is rooted in the Way, and benevolence is indeed the substance of the Way. Learning provides the foundation for government, and the mind is the source of learning. To cultivate the Way through benevolence is to resemble Heaven in its transforming and perfecting activity, bringing abundance to the great enterprise. To direct learning through the mind is to resemble Heaven in its profound, unceasing operation, making the great Way spiritually efficacious. Thus, what accumulates deeply becomes manifest; what is firmly rooted flourishes, and its blossoms emerge…

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
焉絲綸之音秩矣光輝著焉經綸之文宣
矣炳然煥然可以可大而世爲天下法矣
知此則我
太祖高皇帝及我
皇上之文所以布之爲經垂之爲範者有不可
得而揄揚其萬一矣乎請敬陳之夫帝王
之有詔令也所以渙大號而一民之趨也
其有製作也所以明聖學而端物之軌也
四岳之咨勑天之歌載在虞書遐哉邈矣
===
秦漢以降孰其嗣之粵自
天厭胡元篤生
眞主我
太祖高皇帝以聖神之資當貞元之會恢廓氛
祲肇造區宇
功德之隆同符堯舜
文章之盛照耀古今其布之
詔令也
諭安南則曰朕統天下惟願民安而已無强
punctuated:
焉，絲綸之音秩矣；光輝著焉，經綸之文宣矣。炳然煥然，可以可大，而世爲天下法矣。知此，則我太祖高皇帝及我皇上之文，所以布之爲經、垂之爲範者，有不可得而揄揚其萬一矣乎？請敬陳之。
夫帝王之有詔令也，所以渙大號而一民之趨也；其有製作也，所以明聖學而端物之軌也。四岳之咨、勑天之歌，載在虞書，遐哉邈矣！秦漢以降，孰其嗣之？粵自天厭胡元，篤生眞主。我太祖高皇帝以聖神之資，當貞元之會，恢廓氛祲，肇造區宇。功德之隆，同符堯舜；文章之盛，照耀古今。其布之詔令也，諭安南則曰：「朕統天下，惟願民安而已，無强
translation_en:
…therein, and the silken words of imperial pronouncements attain their ordered form; their radiance shines forth, and writings for governing the realm are promulgated. Brilliant and resplendent, they may attain greatness [?] and serve through the ages as a model for all under Heaven. Knowing this, can we adequately praise even one ten-thousandth of what the writings of our Emperor Taizu Gao and our reigning emperor accomplish, disseminated as enduring standards and handed down as models? Permit me respectfully to set this forth.
Emperors and kings issue edicts to broadcast their great commands and unify the direction of their people's endeavors. They compose writings to elucidate sagely learning and set aright the standards for all things. The consultation with the Four Peaks and the song on attending reverently to Heaven's mandate are recorded in the Book of Yu. How distant and remote that age! Since the Qin and Han, who has carried on this tradition? Then Heaven, weary of the non-Han Yuan dynasty, brought forth a true sovereign. Our Emperor Taizu Gao, endowed with sagely and divine qualities, appeared at the juncture of an old cycle's end and a new one's beginning. He swept away the baleful vapors and founded the realm anew. The grandeur of his achievements and virtue matched Yao and Shun; the splendor of his writings illuminated past and present. As for what he promulgated in edicts, in his admonition to Annan he said: “I rule all under Heaven and wish only that the people may live in peace. Let not the strong…

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
陵弱衆暴寡之爲待遐方之夷何仁也
諭雲南則曰人心轉移之機在人自審而已
曰令爾君臣同享承平之福諭梗化之夷
何仁也
赦宥之詔則曰肆赦于眚災爲善良者圖其用
詔則曰朕當會居存養使不失所其用仁廣矣
仁審矣存恤之
曰刑官無私邪政平訟理曰獄清而無事
心靜而神安所以
===
諭刑官也曰爾其所宣□□業其□□□□
慎法獄□□□□罪□人□□□□
命御史也欽恤之誠好生之德蓋讓□達□之
下矣曰天之所以命人主者爲慈民之衆
曰爲朕福民乃受命之利
諭樂到人材也曰倉廩盈府庫充皆民之所
供曰非致吾民于仁壽之鄉將何以荅
天心之未顧
詔免天下秋糧也愛民之眞聚人之惠蓋油然
punctuated:
陵弱、衆暴寡之爲。」待遐方之夷，何仁也！諭雲南則曰：「人心轉移之機，在人自審而已。」曰：「令爾君臣同享承平之福。」諭梗化之夷，何仁也！
赦宥之詔則曰：「肆赦于眚災，爲善良者圖其用。」詔則曰：「朕當會居存養，使不失所。」其用仁廣矣，仁審矣。存恤之曰：「刑官無私邪，政平訟理。」曰：「獄清而無事，心靜而神安。」所以諭刑官也。曰：「爾其所宣□□業其□□□□，慎法獄□□□□罪□人□□□□。」命御史也。欽恤之誠，好生之德，蓋讓□達□之下矣。
曰：「天之所以命人主者，爲慈民之衆。」曰：「爲朕福民，乃受命之利。」諭樂到人材也。曰：「倉廩盈，府庫充，皆民之所供。」曰：「非致吾民于仁壽之鄉，將何以荅天心之未顧？」詔免天下秋糧也。愛民之眞，聚人之惠，蓋油然
translation_en:
…oppressing the weak, or the many brutalizing the few.” How benevolent he was in treating the peoples of distant lands! In instructing Yunnan, he said: “The pivotal moment when people’s hearts change depends simply on their examining themselves.” He also said: “Let you, ruler and ministers alike, enjoy the blessings of enduring peace.” How benevolent he was in instructing peoples who resisted his civilizing influence!
In an edict of pardon, he said: “Extend pardon to inadvertent offenses and misfortunes; devise ways to employ those who are good and upright.” Another edict said: “I shall assemble and settle them, sustain and nurture them [?], so that none loses a place of support.” His exercise of benevolence was broad, and his benevolence discerning. In providing care and relief [?], he said: “When judicial officials are free of selfishness and perversity, government is equitable and lawsuits are properly settled.” He also said: “When the prisons are clear and there is no business, the mind is tranquil and the spirit at ease.” This was how he instructed judicial officials. He said: “You should proclaim … undertakings … exercise care in the laws and imprisonment … offenses … persons … [?].” This was his charge to the investigating censors. His sincerity in reverently attending to punishment with compassion, and his virtue in cherishing life, surely … reached those below [?].
He said: “Heaven appoints rulers in order that they may show compassion to the multitude of the people.” He also said: “Bring blessings to the people on my behalf: this is the benefit of receiving your commission.” This was an instruction concerning men of talent [?]. He said: “The granaries are full and the treasuries well stocked: all this is supplied by the people.” He also said: “Unless I bring my people into a realm of benevolence and longevity, how shall I requite Heaven’s concern [?]?” This was his edict remitting the autumn grain tax throughout the empire. The genuineness of his love for the people and the kindness through which he gathered them to him welled forth spontaneously …

title: 嘉靖二十八年陝西鄉試錄
text:
治下民心矣
天光昭回赫著簡素四岳之咨其道同歸是豈
特感南粤稽首之誠啓河西明見之惘而
已哉其形之
製作也七曜循環之論則曰天大運而左旋一
晝夜一周三百六十五度小運之旋一晝
夜西行一度一年一周天太陽同其數太
陰一晝夜行十三度一月一周天是心達
天道之精矣鬼神有無之論則曰鬼神之
===
事未甞無甚顯而甚寂所以古之哲王立
祀典者以其有之而如是是心契鬼神之
妙矣時令貴正也時雪之論則曰均調四
時其機在乎生靈之主富貴貧賤當有守
思之道其慎脩匪懈之心乎寸陰可惜也
春光之記則曰今春既往學業未周雖有
來春非今之新春也其自强不息之心乎
曰心也者中虛而不實以居神靈曰人之
于世多神役心非心役神問心之擬也曰
punctuated:
治下民心矣。天光昭回，赫著簡素；四岳之咨，其道同歸。是豈特感南粤稽首之誠，啓河西明見之惘而已哉？
其形之製作也，七曜循環之論則曰：「天大運而左旋，一晝夜一周三百六十五度。小運之旋，一晝夜西行一度，一年一周天。太陽同其數，太陰一晝夜行十三度，一月一周天。」是心達天道之精矣。鬼神有無之論則曰：「鬼神之事未甞無，甚顯而甚寂。所以古之哲王立祀典者，以其有之而如是。」是心契鬼神之妙矣。時令貴正也，時雪之論則曰：「均調四時，其機在乎生靈之主。富貴貧賤，當有守思之道。」其慎脩匪懈之心乎！寸陰可惜也，春光之記則曰：「今春既往，學業未周，雖有來春，非今之新春也。」其自强不息之心乎！曰：「心也者，中虛而不實，以居神靈。」曰：「人之于世，多神役心，非心役神。」問心之擬也。曰：
translation_en:
…governs the hearts of the people below [?]. Heavenly radiance shines all around, brilliantly manifest on bamboo slips and silk. The consultation of the Four Peaks accords with the same Way. Could this merely have moved Nanyue to the sincerity of bowing his head, and dispelled Hexi’s bewilderment through clear understanding [?]?
As for its expression in imperial writings, the discourse on the revolutions of the Seven Luminaries states: “Heaven’s great movement turns leftward, completing a circuit of three hundred and sixty-five degrees in one day and night. The rotation of the lesser movement proceeds westward one degree in one day and night, completing a circuit of heaven in one year. The sun follows the same number; the moon travels thirteen degrees in one day and night, completing a circuit of heaven in one month.” This mind comprehends the essence of the Way of Heaven. The discourse on whether ghosts and spirits exist states: “The workings of ghosts and spirits have never been absent: they are supremely manifest yet supremely still. The wise kings of antiquity established the prescribed sacrifices because these beings exist in this manner.” This mind accords with the subtle mystery of ghosts and spirits.
